summary: The little beast in your care is restless, violently trying to carve its place amongst the other children of age.

title: Lust
summary: Your natural inclination for violence has lately assumed a new flavour when you find yourself close to young people of the opposite gender, especially if...

title: Lust: the guardian hears
summary: The little beast in your care has developed an insatiable lust, abusing other children whenever manages to subdue them or, if nothing else is available,...

title: Horns grow
summary: A young male beastman grows horns, sized by his parents.

title: Horns lost in battle
summary: You try to fall back and the enemy's blade strikes true. When you come to your senses again, you realize only a couple of stumps remain where your horns used...

title: The herd attacks
summary: An AI beastman lord at peace attacks a civilised neighbour (beastman_migration CB).

title: A captive is taken
summary: on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The herd pillages
summary: A Chaos lord on a despoilment war takes a civilised capital: raze it, take captives, or pass through. on_siege_over_winner.

title: Our lands are pillaged
summary: The merciless herd of have wrought destruction and ruin in your lands, destroying any building they came across and hunting down people like monsters from...

title: The herd sacks a holding
summary: A beastman who wins a siege of a holding with four or more buildings can sack it for gold and learning (one building burnt, the holder and his top liege furious) or spare it for prestige. The province is then safe from another sack for ten years. Moved from the greenskin file (was WAAGH.9).

title: Captured slaves
summary: Sacrifice a slave at the herdstone, keep them, or let them go.

title: A prisoner is eaten
summary: The court is scared into submission. beastman_eat_prisoner.

title: Herdstone offering: a small horde
summary: Your offering has pleased the gods. A small host of Beastmen, lured in by the lure of trophies and blood, has decided to join your herd.

title: Herdstone offering: a large horde
summary: Your offering has pleased the gods. A large host of Beastmen, lured in by the promise of war and slaughter, has decided to join your herd.

title: Herdstone offering: giants
summary: Your offering has pleased the gods. A band of trolls and giants have wandered into your domain and have found a temporary home around your herdstone, joining...

title: Herdstone offering: raiders
summary: Raiders rise at the capital (beastmen.67).

title: Raiders rise
summary: A rebel warherd rises at the capital.

title: Raise a beastman retinue (elite)
summary: The herd has grown, and the mightiest beasts of the forest answer the call of the brayhorn. Which of them will march at your side?

title: Raise a beastman retinue
summary: Young gors gather at the herdstone, eager to prove themselves. Which of them will join your warherd?

title: Raise a Chaos retinue (elite)
summary: For Kurgan and Hung Chaos lords.

title: Raise a Chaos retinue
summary: For Kurgan and Hung Chaos lords.

title: The conquered rise
summary: A beastman lord holding civilised provinces faces a peasant revolt in one of them (beastmen.76).

title: Peasants rise
summary: Peasant rebels spawn and declare war on the top liege.

title: Lieges hear of the revolt
summary: The weak inhabitants have risen up in , led by a determined leader wanting to reclaim this land for their pitiable kind.

title: Too many clan titles
summary: Deactivates one of two clan titles held by a beastman ruler. Meant for on_inheritance but not hooked up (Komi, 2026-10-27: leave it unused).

title: Small but deadly
summary: A halfling with two daggers ambushes a beastman lord whose lands touch the Moot, or any beastman leading troops into the Moot or besieging a holding there. Fight (a martial gamble), bellow for the herd, or, for a bray shaman, curse the wretch. At most once every two years per character. by on_unit_entering_province and on_siege_pulse (random: beastmen_moot_ambush).

title: The Chaos moon
summary: Clears last year's full moon, or rolls for a new one: about once in 25 years, more often as the doom rises. Players hear of it (beastmen.86).

title: Morrslieb waxes
summary: The Chaos moon hangs full and green above the forest, and the herdstones hum. Every beast in the woods feels it: the hunger, the fury, the call of the Dark...

title: The shaman reads the signs
summary: Picks the omen and the shaman who reads it: a courtier, else a vassal, else the ruler.

title: The gods ask for blood
summary: Attack a civilised neighbour, or take the omen's fury into the next fight. Turning the gods down costs piety.

title: The herdstone sings
summary: The capital's herdstone hums with power. Gather the herd for a great rite, or feast.

title: Bad signs
summary: The entrails are black. The shaman asks for a sacrifice: a prisoner, gold, or nothing, and the herd's spirit sinks for two years.

title: The journey begins
summary: The pilgrim says farewell and sets off for the Heart of the Dark.

title: Planning the route
summary: Sets how many road events the journey has: two from near the Drakwald, three from further away, four from the far corners of the world. Distance is measured from Marienburg (province 222), at the edge of the forest.

calls: brayherd.10; brayherd.11; brayherd.12; brayherd.13; brayherd.14; brayherd.15; brayherd.19; brayherd.20; brayherd.4
title: Road event roll
summary: Picks one road event the pilgrim has not had yet. When the road events are used up, or none fits, the pilgrim reaches the Heart of the Dark (brayherd.4).

title: The Heart of the Dark
summary: The pilgrim arrives. Two events at the Heart of the Dark follow.

title: Smoke over the trees
summary: The warband stumbles on a human hamlet in the forest. Burn it, drag the survivors to the Herdstone as sacrifices (pleases the Herdstone most), or leave it and keep the pace.

title: A challenger in the warband
summary: A young gor of the pilgrim's own warband challenges for the leadership, as beastmen do. Fight him (better odds with martial skill, duelists and the brave), let the bestigors kill him (costs prestige), or, for the cunning, send him to lead a raid that goes wrong.

title: The Dark Omen
summary: Malagor, the crow-winged bray-shaman, reads the pilgrim's fate. Letting him read the entrails gives a good or ill omen (beastmen_blood_omen or beastmen_ill_omen); a sacrifice buys better odds; driving him off angers the Herdstone.

title: The Brass Bull
summary: Taurox, the Doombull of brass flesh, crashes past on an endless rampage. Join it (glory, wounds or worse; pleases the Herdstone), steer the minotaurs at a human town (cunning pilgrims), or get out of the way.

title: The drunken centigors
summary: A band of centigors, half-horse and wholly drunk, staggers into camp with stolen wine. Drink with them (they may ride along and boast of the pilgrim, or leave him with a habit), race their chief, or drive them off.

title: A warlord's invitation
summary: An AI beastman king or emperor (a rival if there is one) invites the pilgrim to his camp. Accept (brayherd.16), use it to murder a rival (schemers, brayherd.18) or keep to your own tent.

title: The warlord's feast
summary: Usually a good rest. A host who is not yet a friend may become one; a rival host may poison the pilgrim (eight times likelier if deceitful): half the time that kills, half the time it ends in brayherd.17.

title: Waking in a ditch
summary: The poisoned pilgrim survives with food poisoning (or poisoned, without Reapers) and a warning to stay away.

title: Fatal hospitality
summary: A schemer's murder attempt on the rival host: a clean kill and escape (more likely with high intrigue), a kill that costs the pilgrim's life, or a failure that does. Pilgrims who cannot die carry on with the journey.

title: A knight in the thorns
summary: The warband drags a knight of the man-things out of a thorn thicket, lost and alone. Save him for the Herdstone (the best offering), sell him back to his kin, or throw him in the fighting pit for sport.

title: Tracks of a Jabberslythe
summary: The pilgrim finds the work of a great Jabberslythe and can hunt it (brayherd.21). Hunters always do.

title: How the hunt goes
summary: Even odds: the pilgrim corners the beast (brayherd.23), meets a rival hunter (brayherd.22) or gets lost (brayherd.24).

title: The other hunter
summary: A lone bestigor hunts the same beast. Take him into your court (better odds at the kill), leave him be, or treat him as a rival (worse odds, and the pilgrim grows cruel and paranoid).

title: The Jabberslythe cornered
summary: Fighting gives prestige and a roll: mastery of the hunt, a wound, the beast escaping, maiming or death. A hunting companion makes mastery likelier, a slain rival maiming and death. Fleeing costs prestige and courage.

title: Lost in the forest
summary: The pilgrim wanders lost for weeks: may fall ill (if healthy), and may become stressed, depressed or wroth.

title: Heart of the Dark event roll
summary: Picks one event the pilgrim has not had yet at the Heart of the Dark. When they are used up, or none fits, the rite at the Herdstone follows (brayherd.39).

title: The fighting ring
summary: Bestigors brawl in a ring. Duelists win money and pride; others can try their luck. Fighting pleases the Herdstone; watching and betting does not.

title: The shrine of a single god
summary: Bestigors worship one Chaos god at a defiled altar. Joining in may make the pilgrim cynical or turn them to that god; an undivided pilgrim can denounce them (piety, but the Herdstone frowns); or study their symbols.

title: The herd market
summary: A market of meat, slaves and plunder. Feast (may turn gluttonous), buy a beastman artifact, or steal one (intrigue 15 or elusive shadow).

title: Before the Great Herdstone
summary: Ends the pilgrimage. The rite's outcome is rolled from the favour gathered on the journey plus half the pilgrim's diplomacy, rank and the Brayherd's opinion: a bad rite (favour 100 for those who humble themselves, at a cost in prestige), an okay one (favour 150) or a great one (favour 300, piety, martial and health).

title: A bray shaman for the court
summary: Boon: the Brayherd's governor sends a bray shaman (wizard, often marked by a god or a mutation) to serve as court physician. Stronger while the Brayherd is united. Announced by brayherd.51.

title: The bray shaman arrives
summary: Letter from the governor; the shaman becomes court physician.

title: A war leader for the court
summary: Boon: the governor sends a scarred bestigor of the ruler's god to lead the armies (strategist modifier, commander if a slot is free). Announced by brayherd.53.

title: The war leader arrives
summary: Letter from the governor; the bestigor becomes a commander if possible.

title: A daemonic artifact
summary: Boon: a random beastman artifact the ruler does not own yet.

title: A gift of Chaos
summary: Boon: a mutation (hides, runes, tusks, senses, limbs) or a bigger set of horns, up to a crown of horns. About one roll in six brings nothing visible. Every roll counts towards the mutation counter.

title: A request for a bray
summary: Boon: the governor picks a bride for a male ruler or relative, either from his own bloodline or a lowborn beauty, and gives her family, looks and a personality (abler while the Brayherd is united). Then brayherd.61. The decision only allows male grooms, so the bride is always created. FROMFROMFROM the groom.

title: The bride is on her way
summary: Letter to the ruler who asked; the bride arrives in two to three weeks.

title: The bride arrives
summary: The bride and groom can marry again; the wedding follows (brayherd.63).

title: A ruinous union
summary: The groom takes the bride as consort: prestige (more if she is of the Brayherd's own blood) and, for a ruler who married himself, five years of peace with the Brayherd. Tells the ruler who asked (brayherd.64).

title: The wedding is announced
summary: Tells the ruler who arranged a relative's wedding: 25 years of peace with the Brayherd.

title: The call is made
summary: Ten years after a lord claimed the right to call a Black Crusade: if no war was declared, the claim lapses (bcrusade.2). decision in wh_chaos_decisions.txt, 3650 days later.

title: The claim lapses
summary: Hidden. A lord who holds the right to call a Black Crusade (title flag temp_religion_head) loses it again, unless he claimed it less than ten years ago, is preparing a Black Crusade or is fighting one. (wh_on_actions), by bcrusade.1, bcrusade.22 and the CBs when the war ends.

title: The cooldown begins
summary: Hidden. When a Black Crusade ends, that god may not call another for thirty years, or a hundred for a low-doom crusade. The timers are title flags on k_cult_of_sigmar. new_crusade CBs in 00_cb_types.

title: The cooldown ends
summary: Hidden. Clears Black Crusade timers older than thirty (or a hundred) years. can_call_black_crusade also treats such old timers as expired, so a Black Crusade can come again even with no Grand Theogonist.

title: Other lords are off limits
summary: Hidden. While a Black Crusade runs, every other independent ruler is flagged so the call CB does not show against them. on_crusade_monthly.

title: Lords are fair game again
summary: Hidden. Clears the flags bcrusade.5 set. CBs.

title: The chosen lord
summary: Hidden. Picks the official recipient of the target lands: the faithful holder, his heir, or a claimant the warlord likes. With nobody fit, pledged lords fall back to their own beneficiaries, and the horde is told by letter (bcrusade.130, .131). on_crusade_target_changes, and by bcrusade.11 and .12.

title: The chosen lord turns away
summary: Hidden. If the official recipient no longer follows the god of the crusade, a new one is picked (bcrusade.10).

title: The chosen lord dies
summary: Hidden. If the official recipient dies, a new one is picked (bcrusade.10).

title: Preparation begins
summary: Hidden. Tells every ruler of the faith that a Black Crusade is being prepared (bcrusade.14).

title: The faithful prepare for war
summary: The warlord asks for warriors against the target. A lord may pledge at once or wait.

title: The first pledges
summary: Hidden. AI rulers of the faith may pledge at the start, more often the zealous, the great and those whose lands lie in the target realm.

title: More pledges
summary: Hidden. While the horde is weaker than the defence, more AI lords are asked each month, the most zealous first.

title: An AI lord pledges
summary: Hidden. An AI lord pledges, adds to the war chest, and names a beneficiary for the lands: a kinsman with a claim, a child, another of his house, or nobody. CBs.

title: The Black Crusade marches
summary: Hidden. Announces the launch (bcrusade.19) and takes holy orders out of the war chest.

title: Black Crusade for the target
summary: The launch, seen by every ruler. The text says whether the target was once Chaos land (the Wastes, Norsca), on its fringe (the Darklands) or never held. Lords who promised the Forces of Order their help are called to the defence (bcrusade.25).

title: Called to the defence
summary: Hidden. A lord who promised to fight the Black Crusade joins the defender's wars, with an alliance and good opinion both ways.

title: No launch
summary: Hidden. The Black Crusade was cancelled: the faith is told (bcrusade.21) and its authority suffers.

title: The target turned
summary: The target secretly worshipped Chaos and has declared it; the horde must choose another.

title: The target falls to Chaos
summary: Hidden. If the target lands come into Chaos hands before the launch, the crusade is called off and its timers start (bcrusade.2, .3, .6).

title: Debts called in
summary: Hidden. The AI warlord makes an AI lord who owes him a favour pledge.

title: A debt called in
summary: Hidden. The warlord writes to a player who owes him a favour (bcrusade.32).

title: The warlord's letter
summary: A player who owes the warlord a favour is told to march.

title: Pledged
summary: Hidden. When a player pledges, one of bcrusade.41-45 may follow. on_pledge_crusade_participation.

title: A courtier approves
summary: A courtier is glad of the pledge.

title: Another lord approves
summary: Another pledged lord writes in approval; two zealots become friends.

title: A rival offers peace
summary: A rival marching in the same horde offers to end the feud.

title: The blood stirs
summary: The player feels the gods' call and becomes zealous.

title: A farewell to the old friend
summary: A mad lord says goodbye to the thing in the lake, or in the woods. supernatural events on.

title: Unpledged
summary: Hidden. When a player breaks the pledge, one of bcrusade.51-54 may follow.

title: A courtier is disgusted
summary: A courtier tells the player what they think of the broken pledge.

title: Another lord is displeased
summary: Another pledged lord writes in disgust.

title: A new rival
summary: Another pledged lord declares the player a rival.

title: Cast out
summary: Hidden. The warlord casts out the oath-breaker (trait excommunicated) and tells the faith (bcrusade.55).

title: Traitor to the gods
summary: The faith hears who broke the pledge.

title: The warlord writes
summary: Hidden. The warlord asks a player who has not pledged (bcrusade.61).

title: The warlord's summons
summary: Pledge, pay a year's income instead, or wait.

title: Beneficiaries checked
summary: Hidden. Each month, a beneficiary who died, got land, became an heir, a mercenary, a monk or too sick is dropped. AI lords pick a new one (bcrusade.17); players are told why (bcrusade.120). bcrusade.63). Fired from on_crusade_monthly and by bcrusade.63.

title: A beneficiary dies or is landed
summary: Hidden. Marks why, and has the warlord recheck (bcrusade.62).

title: The new lord of the conquered land
summary: A player may play on as the new ruler of the conquered realm. Fired by the new_crusade CB in 00_cb_types.

title: Pledges that no longer stand
summary: Hidden. Lords at war with the warlord, or no longer of the faith or landed, lose their pledge.

title: Taken back
summary: Hidden. A cast-out lord who pledges is forgiven by letter (bcrusade.67). .61, and by pledge_crusade_effect.

title: Forgiven
summary: The warlord lifts the curse on a lord who has come back to the horde.

title: The beneficiary's new land
summary: Hidden. Prepares bcrusade.71.

title: The lord in the conquered land
summary: A player whose beneficiary got a county in the conquered realm may play on as the beneficiary.

title: Defence pledges
summary: Hidden. Rulers of the target's faith, and Old World, Dawi, Ormazd, halfling and Cathay rulers when the target is one of them, may pledge to the defence (bcrusade.81). More do so near the target, when doom is high, or when the Everchosen walks. by bcrusade.82.

title: A defence pledge
summary: Hidden. A ruler of the target's faith pledges to the defence; other faiths promise to join when the horde marches (flag forces_of_order_defender, used by bcrusade.19). Kings and emperors write to the target (bcrusade.85).

title: A new target
summary: Hidden. If the target changes to a ruler of another faith, defence pledges are sought again (bcrusade.80).

title: The defence is outmatched
summary: Hidden. When the horde is far stronger, more of the target's faith come to help.

title: Debts to the defender
summary: Hidden. An AI ruler who owes the target a favour pledges to the defence.

title: A promise of help
summary: The target hears that a king of the faith will stand by them.

title: The first offerings
summary: Hidden. The warlord puts half his treasury, piety, prestige and four artifacts in the war chest.

title: Gold for the war
summary: Hidden. AI rulers of the faith who do not march are asked to pay (bcrusade.92).

title: A gift of gold
summary: Hidden. An AI ruler gives a year's income or more, by zeal.

title: Gold for the marchers
summary: Hidden. A fifth of the war chest's gold goes out at the launch.

title: A siege won
summary: Hidden. Each siege won by the horde fills the war chest.

title: A battle won
summary: Hidden. Each battle won by the horde fills the war chest. hooks.

title: No spoils for holy orders
summary: Hidden. Holy orders get no share of the war chest.

title: A new master
summary: Hidden. When an order gets a new master, bcrusade.96 runs again.

title: A gift to the war chest
summary: A lord gives one, two or four years of income for piety. donate decision).

title: The army comes home
summary: Hidden. Refills levies and lifts the bad modifiers from the realm after a crusade. that end.

title: Who gets the land
summary: A pledged lord chooses: the warlord's chosen lord, his own beneficiary, or himself if he did most.

title: Why the beneficiary was dropped
summary: Hidden. Sends the right notice (bcrusade.121-128).

title: Beneficiary dead
summary: Notice.

title: Beneficiary landed
summary: Notice.

title: Beneficiary an heir
summary: Notice.

title: Beneficiary a mercenary
summary: Notice.

title: Beneficiary in a holy order
summary: Notice.

title: Beneficiary too young
summary: Notice.

title: Beneficiary sick
summary: Notice.

title: Beneficiary took vows
summary: Notice.

title: A new chosen lord
summary: The warlord names a new chosen lord for the lands.

title: No chosen lord
summary: The warlord names nobody: the lords decide with their swords.

title: Lords who did not pledge
summary: Hidden. At the launch, players who refused the summons are rebuked (bcrusade.141).

title: The warlord's scorn
summary: Piety lost and the warlord's anger; a king may be cast out.

title: Shirkers watched
summary: Hidden. A year after the launch the warlord looks for lords who pledged and never fought (bcrusade.151).

title: First letters
summary: Hidden. Writes to shirkers (bcrusade.152) and looks again a year later (bcrusade.153).

title: A first warning
summary: A shirker loses piety and the warlord's goodwill.

title: Second letters
summary: Hidden. Writes to those still shirking (bcrusade.154).

title: A last warning
summary: A shirker who ignored the first letter is cast out.

title: Victory
summary: Every ruler hears who won the Black Crusade and who took the land.

title: The last of the house
summary: Hidden. When the last lord of a house who got crusade land dies, the dynasty modifier goes.

title: Clean-up
summary: Hidden. Clears the global and character flags of a finished crusade.

title: The duchy is ours
summary: The lord has taken the last stronghold of a duchy. Give it to his chosen lord (or a fitting kinsman) as a tributary realm, take it for himself (the other crusaders resent it), abdicate his old realm to his heir and rule it in person, or let it go for the prestige and gold the decision cost. dynamic_crusader_state (event targets duchy_region, crusader_lord).

title: A lord settles in his dominion
summary: Narrative for players: the lord left his old realm to rule the dominion himself. The heir may switch to play him.

title: A new dominion
summary: Narrative for players: the warlord's chosen lord now rules the dominion. The warlord, if a kinsman, may switch to play the new lord.

title: A selfish conquest
summary: Narrative for players: a lord took the dominion for himself.

title: The old dominion title
summary: A ruler holding a made-up dominion duchy and a real higher title can make the made-up title the true duchy, let it go for a claim on the real one, or keep it. on_new_holder_inheritance and on_new_holder_usurpation.

title: The monthly campaign roll
summary: Hidden. Once a month of a Black Crusade, each pledged commander in enemy land rolls crusade_flavor_event_tombola_effect (crusadefl.1-15).

title: A fellow warlord's camp
summary: A player passes the camp of another lord sworn to the Black Crusade, who invites him to share his fire.

title: Strange lands
summary: The commander spends some days among a foreign people. He can study them, befriend one of them, shut them out, or, once he knows them well and is of a kindred race, take up their ways.

title: The field of the dead
summary: The host crosses an old battlefield. The commander can bury his own, bury everyone, take trophies for the gods, or rob the dead.

title: The merchant caravan
summary: A caravan offers the commander a piece of regalia from its homeland. He can buy it, take it by the sword, rob the traders, or ride on. The piece depends on the faith of the land (wh_black_crusade_effects.txt). Rare: once a lifetime, and only if the commander has not bought from one before.

title: Far from home
summary: The long march weighs on the commander. He presses on, eases off, or leans on his god.

title: The twin-tailed comet
summary: A comet crosses the night sky and the camp reads it as a sign. Seen twice, a sign and a firm hand together make the commander hear a voice of battle.

title: Heads on the road
summary: Some of the host behead locals for their faith. The commander joins in, condemns it, or calls it a needed lesson.

title: The hidden faithful
summary: Deep in enemy land, a few locals of the commander's own faith take the host in. He can pay to spread the faith there, take one of them home, or just thank them.

title: The cutpurse
summary: A street boy steals the commander's purse. He laughs it off, hunts the boy down, or takes him into service.

title: The hedge sorcerer
summary: The commander visits a local sorcerer. He learns from him, or kills him and takes his books. Khornates lose zeal for it; mages gain magic experience; the gifted may wake to a lore.

title: The old festival
summary: The host comes upon a festival to old gods. The commander joins in, keeps apart, or loses himself in it.

title: A voice in the night
summary: After a long night of drink, the commander hears his god tell him to give all to the war. He obeys, blames the wine, or, if he is zealous and holy enough, gives up his lands to take the vows of a holy order of his faith.

title: Riders of the order
summary: Knights of a holy order of the commander's faith share his camp, and their master asks him to sit up and talk. A friend, or an insult.

title: The tavern
summary: A serving girl or boy in a tavern takes an interest in the commander. He sends them off, takes one night, or brings them home as a lover.

title: The men are restless
summary: A long halt sours the host. The commander drills them or fires them up; done twice over each, he becomes a great general.

title: The horde is broken
summary: Hidden. A Black Crusade has failed. Marks the kingdom the warlord came from and, in one to three years, a province of the defender's faith where a prophet will preach. on_reverse_demand of new_crusade.

title: The prophet preaches
summary: Hidden. A doom-prophet starts to preach in the marked province. Players of its faith hear of it (bcrusade.302); the host sets out a year or two later (bcrusade.303).

title: The prophet of doom
summary: Narrative for players of the province's faith: a prophet is stirring the commons, and the lords are too weary to stop him.

title: The Penitent Host marches
summary: Hidden. The prophet raises his host (a landless adventurer title, nine thousand men) and declares war on the ruler who holds the most of the kingdom the Black Crusade came from. Players hear of it (bcrusade.304).

title: The Penitent Host
summary: Narrative for every player: the host sets out. Its own faithful marvel, everyone else scoffs.

title: The host is broken
summary: Narrative for every player: the host lost its war. shepherds_crusade_invasion CB (on_reverse_demand).

title: The Penitent Kingdom
summary: Narrative for every player: the host won, and its prophet is a king. shepherds_crusade_invasion CB (on_success_title).

title: The prophet is dead
summary: Narrative for every player: the prophet fell and the host scatters. shepherds_crusade_invasion CB (on_attacker_leader_death).

calls: bcrusade.311; bcrusade.312; bcrusade.313; bcrusade.314; bcrusade.315; bcrusade.316
title: The host on the road
summary: Hidden. As the host enters a province, something happens there, at most once every fifty days per lord. In lands of the host's faith, locals join it, or the lord is asked for help (.311), to drive out the Strigany (.312), to bear its disorder (.313) or its deserters (.314), or it burns a priest who spoke against it (.315). In other lands it brings disorder (.316) or the downtrodden of its faith rise to join it. on_unit_entering_province.

title: The host at the gates

title: General Winter
summary: Hidden. A foreign commander marches into a Kislevite province in winter, at war with its lord: the province turns hostile with cold (supply and attrition) for three months, and he may fall ill. Kislevites, the peoples of the Wastes and Norsca, the dead and daemons do not feel it.

title: Call the Winter
summary: An Ice Witch calls an early winter on the enemies in her lord's Kislevite lands (decision bulwark_call_winter). The besieged and occupied provinces freeze for half a year. One time in three the cold comes home too: a famine at her lord's capital.

title: The Spring Driving comes
summary: Hidden. Picks the chieftain: the lord's old nemesis if he still lives, otherwise a new one from a Kurgan court (or a Chaos court of the Wastes).

title: The Spring Driving
summary: The chieftain's riders come over the river into the lord's lands. Ride out to meet them (a fight, and a chance to kill him), hold the stanitsa walls (a Frost Ward helps; if it holds it becomes a Stanitsa of Heroes), or pay them to ride on. A burned stanitsa sends refugees south (bulwark.12). event_target:spring_province the province raided.

title: Refugees from the north
summary: The burned stanitsa's people come south with what they could carry. Settle them in the lord's capital (more hands and taxes, more unrest), or turn them away.

title: The chieftain falls
summary: The lord cuts down the chieftain who led the Spring Driving. His skull-torc can be taken, once in a lifetime, and the Wastes are a little weaker.

title: The Motherland Calls
summary: Hidden. A Black Crusade falls on a Kislevite realm: its ruler and every Kislevite lord of the realm take heart (morale, levy reinforcement, less revolt) until the war ends. The first time the Tsardom itself is the target, the Oath of Karaz brings the Dwarfs (bulwark.25).

title: The Motherland Calls
summary: Notice for the ruler under the Black Crusade.

title: The Crusade is broken
summary: The Black Crusade against Kislev has failed. Great prestige, and the doom of the world falls back.

title: The Crusade ends
summary: Hidden. The war with the Black Crusade ended in its victory or a white peace: the Motherland Calls ends.

title: The Oath of Karaz
summary: The first time a Black Crusade falls on the Tsardom, the Dwarfs of the World's Edge keep the old oath for the passes near Praag: a Dwarf captain and a small host come to the Tzar(ina) until the peace.

title: The Siege of Praag
summary: Hidden. A Chaos army has Praag under siege. Praag's lord is asked about a sortie (bulwark.31); the breach comes a month later (bulwark.32), and if Praag still stands in half a year it holds (bulwark.34).

title: A sortie from Praag
summary: The hordes are at the walls of Praag. Lead a sortie out of the north gate (glory or wounds), or keep the walls.

title: The breach
summary: The wall is down by the north gate. A hero of the court holds the breach to the last (bulwark.33), or the lord fights there himself.

title: The last stand at the breach
summary: The hero holds the breach until the wall is shored up behind him, and dies there. Praag sings of him.

title: Praag holds
summary: Half a year after the Chaos siege began, Praag is still in the hands of its lord and free of the siege. Great prestige, and a cut to doom.

title: A great city falls
summary: Hidden. A Chaos army takes Kislev, Praag or Erengrad: the doom of the world rises (minor; medium for Kislev itself).

title: Chaos crosses the Lynsk
summary: Hidden. A Chaos commander enters the Lynsk lands at war with the ruler of the Tsardom, who must choose how to meet him (bulwark.41).

title: The Lynsk Line
summary: The hordes are across the Lynsk. Hold the river (its forts stand stronger, but the levies bleed), or pull back to the cities, burn the land behind you and raise a fresh host (bulwark.42).

title: A fresh host
summary: Half a year after the pull-back, a fresh host is ready at the capital.

title: A stanitsa under siege
summary: Hidden. A Chaos army besieges a holding in northern Kislev whose lord is a Kislevite count with a liege. The liege must answer (bulwark.46).

title: The Last Stand of the Stanitsa
summary: A small garrison in the north is holding against a whole horde to buy the realm time. Ride to relieve it (glory or wounds, and its lord's love), or let it fall (the time it bought strengthens the realm; its lord does not forget). event_target:stand_province the province.

title: Dwarf rangers
summary: Rangers from the World's Edge come down to fight: a small elite company.

title: Volunteers from the Empire
summary: A free company of Ostland and Talabecland men crosses the border to fight.

title: The Gryphon Legion rides home
summary: The Legion comes back from the Empire to fight for Kislev, for free.

title: A wandering Grail Knight
summary: A Grail Knight of Bretonnia who heard of the war rides in and offers his lance. He joins the court.

title: An Ice Witch coven
summary: A coven of Ice Witches freezes the camps of the enemy in the realm's Kislevite lands.

title: Ursun's bears
summary: Wild bears come out of the woods at night and fall on the Chaos camp. The enemy's commanders may be mauled.

title: The White Wolf company
summary: The Knights of the White Star ride from Erengrad to fight beside the realm. They are Ulricans, and the priests of Ursun do not like it.

title: A High Elf mage
summary: An Asur mage who came on the Erengrad ships offers to stand with the realm for the war: he joins the court, and his magic breaks the enemy's nerve. Erengrad.

title: The Strigany warn of a night raid
summary: Strigany travellers bring word of a night attack, and the realm's armies are ready for it. A small favour is owed.

title: The Tzar's Call
summary: Envoys from Kislev (decision bulwark_tzars_call) ask a power of order for help against Chaos. Join the war, send a host under a captain of your own, send gold, or refuse. The AI weighs opinion, distance, its own wars, faith, doom, and old debts. Helpers win the Shield of the North (Kislev's opinion for thirty years) and prestige.

title: An answer to the Call
summary: Notice: a power has answered the Call with men or gold.

title: Brothers in the North
summary: The ruler of Kislev offers the Emperor the old treaty (decision bulwark_brothers_in_the_north): an alliance between the two crowns. Accept or refuse.

title: The brothers are sworn
summary: Notice: the Emperor has sworn the treaty.

title: The Emperor's call
summary: The Empire faces Chaos and the Emperor calls on Kislev (decision bulwark_emperors_call). Old debts make refusal costly.

title: A champion of Chaos slain
summary: Hidden. A Kislevite ruler or a member of the Circle of the Bear kills a Chaos champion, chosen or daemon prince: the doom of the world falls back a little, and the killer hears of it (bulwark.81).

title: The champion is dead
summary: is dead, and you killed him. One less champion of the Ruinous Powers walks the world. The priests of Ursun will hear of it before nightfall.

title: The Gate holds
summary: Once a decade, if Kislev, Praag and Erengrad are all held by Kislev's gods, the wall stands and doom falls back a little.

title: The Tzar falls to Chaos
summary: Hidden. The ruler of Kislev is killed by a follower of Chaos: the doom of the world rises, and a great boyar claims the crown.

title: A bear of Urskin's blood
summary: The Tzar's bear-master brings out a great bear of the line of Urskin, the bear that Tzar Boris rode. One per Tzar: it serves its rider and dies with him, or goes back to the wilds (kislevnorth.2).

title: Hidden. The rider of Urskin's bear dies: the bear lies down
summary: on his grave and dies too, or goes back into the forests around Kislev (a province modifier there for ten years). It never passes to an heir.

title: The caravan from the east
summary: A caravan comes down the High Pass from Cathay with jade, silk, spices and ivory. Escort it (gold, a chance of raiders, kislevnorth.11), tax it hard (more gold, a chance that Cathay's merchants shun the road, kislevnorth.12), or let it pass freely (Praag's trade grows for five years).

title: Raiders on the Pass
summary: Ogres or greenskins fall on the caravan in the Pass. Ride to its rescue (martial: loot and prestige, or the escort fee lost), or let them have it.

title: Cathay shuns the Pass
summary: Word of the Praag tolls has reached the merchants of Cathay, and the caravans go round by the south for ten years. No caravan comes in that time, and Praag's trade suffers.

title: The Kreml Guard swears
summary: The captain of the Kreml Guard kneels before the Tzar(ina) and swears the guard's oath in person. For as long as they reign the guard protects them against knives in the dark. Comes when the guard is founded and with each new holder of the crown.

title: The Kossars come home
summary: Ten years after the company was hired out to a southern prince, the Kossars come home: veterans who make the levies better, gold from the south, or a long list of the dead.

title: A letter from the Kossars
summary: The Kossar captain writes from the south: a siege in Tilea, a battle in the Border Princes, a prince who is slow to pay.

title: Longships on the coast
summary: Norscan longships come in to the coast to raid. Fight them on the shore (martial; a captured jarl, kislevnorth.41, or a burned coast), pay them off, or ambush them at sea with Erengrad's ships.

title: The captured jarl
summary: The raiders are broken and their jarl is in chains. Ransom him to his people (gold), bring him to Ursun (he joins the court on Kislev's faith), or keep him as a hostage (no Norscan raids on this coast for ten years).

title: Trolls in the thaw
summary: In the far north the trolls come down with the thaw. Hunt it (martial; a rare troll-hide cloak, once a lifetime; or a wound, and the troll heals and comes back, kislevnorth.51), pay troll-hunters, or bar the gates.

title: The troll comes back
summary: The troll that was cut down a year ago has grown its arm back and is eating the herds again. Burn it this time, or call on the Circle of the Bear.

title: Hidden. Kislev builds tall
summary: Once an AI Tzar(ina) holds all of Kislev's de jure lands, the crown turns from conquest to defence: a hidden trait lowers ambition and raises zeal, so the AI weakens Chaos and the beasts on its borders and builds at home rather than marching on its neighbours. Removed again if the realm loses de jure land.

title: The Carnival takes to the road
summary: Hidden. Picks a rural town in the ruler's lands, creates the Carnival Master (a secret sorcerer of Nurgle in a fine mask) and his troupe (a Tainted One and a Brute, Nurglite humans) and sends the arrival. More likely when the doom is high and for players. carnival_of_chaos.

title: Painted wagons
summary: The Carnival stops outside a town of the ruler's and promises a play. Welcome them, have them watched, turn them away or arrest the lot. The text changes with the land: an Empire burgher fair, a Tilean commedia troupe, an Estalian fiesta, Bretonnian mummers or Kislevite wandering players.

title: Empty cells
summary: The arrested players die in the night of a bloating sickness, the gaolers sicken, and the painted wagon and its Master are gone. The Carnival moves on.

title: The omens begin
summary: Hidden. Sends one omen the host has not had yet (carnival.11-14). After two omens the play comes (carnival.20). If the truth was seen, the camp can be raided before the show (carnival.25).

title: Sour milk
summary: The milk sours in the pail, the butter will not come and the dogs howl all night at the wagons. Look into it or let it be. A Strigany realm can blame the Strigany instead: easy, and wrong.

title: Flies, flies
summary: A child of the town wakes screaming from a dream of a fat, laughing grandfather, saying "Flies, flies, eat up his eyes!". Then other children have the same dream.

title: The jester's touch
summary: The watcher saw a jester take a girl's hand while he joked with her. By morning she has a weeping sore. Look into it, or burn the sore out and say nothing.

title: The Dance of Death
summary: At dusk a line of townsfolk dances behind the piper, three times round the town, laughing. Not all of them come home. (White Dwarf 119: the night before the attack, three circuits round the village.)

title: What the watcher found
summary: The watcher reports. A seer (witch hunter, wizard, Ice Witch, Grail Knight, Damsel), a sharp spymaster or a sharp ruler may see through the paint: then the camp can be raided before the show. Otherwise nothing is found.

title: The play
summary: The big night: a crude, funny, filthy piece that mocks the ruler. The play changes with the land (The Emperor's True Face, Orfeo and Pustulate, A Midsummer Nightmare, Papa Noigul's Festering Children). Laugh along (the jesters' touch may infect the court), walk out, look closer, or watch the Master instead of the stage. Sunset follows (carnival.30).

title: Grandfather's gift
summary: Between the acts the Master comes to the ruler's seat and offers a gift from Grandfather Nurgle: the patron's bond (a secret fall to Nurgle, doom up, once in a life a Plague Cart). Refuse him, or seize him before sunset.

title: Where shall we play next
summary: The new patron chooses where the Carnival goes next: a rival, an enemy, or wherever the road leads. The town is spared, and the Carnival leaves.

title: Before the show
summary: The truth was seen in time. Burn the wagons at dawn (the Master flees), storm the camp with the guard, or call in the witch hunters. Ice Witches, Grail Knights and paid Tilean blades give their own options.

title: Sunset
summary: The paint runs and the costumes split: Plaguebearers chanting their count, Nurglings spilling from the Plague Cart, the Tainted laughing. Fight (better if forewarned), fire the wagons, flee and seal the town, or bargain with the Master. The Master shows his true faith.

title: The square is held
summary: The daemons are driven back into the Cart and the Brethren cut down. The Master flees with the last wagons: the hunt can begin (carnival.40).

title: The town is lost
summary: The square is lost, or the gates were sealed on the living. The plague takes the town, women and children of the court are led away with a finger missing, and the Carnival moves on.

title: The Master ascends
summary: Rare and once per game (carnival.30 rolls it; only on a lost sunset). On the bodies of the town the Master is raised to a Daemon Prince of Nurgle and forges a small realm: the town's county and up to two of its neighbours break away under him, with a daemon host to hold them. His troupe stays at his court. The doom rises, the host keeps claims on the lost counties, and the Carnival is over.

title: The Master taken
summary: The Master is in chains, or dead in the dust. Burn him (doom falls, the Master's mask may be taken), or give him to the witch hunters (piety). Ends the Carnival.

title: The Master flees
summary: The Master is gone with the last wagons. Hunt him across the land, or let him go to plague someone else.

title: One town behind
summary: Up to three steps of the chase, always a town behind: an emptied village, a field of fingers, a child singing the Master's song. Press on (a roll that may corner him, carnival.42) or give up.

title: The Plague Cart
summary: The Master is cornered at the Cart, chalking the pentagram that opens onto Grandfather's garden. Face him yourself, or send the guard.

summary: Hidden. Clears the old host's flags and sends the Carnival to the next realm: the patron's choice if there is one, else a lord two provinces away. After three realms, or if the Master is dead or taken, or no host is found, it ends (carnival.90).

summary: Word reaches the old host that the painted wagons are now in another lord's lands.

summary: Hidden. Ends the chain: a living, free Master walks off the map, the global flag and targets are cleared, and a new Carnival may start in some later decade.

summary: Word to a player patron that the Carnival has reached the next realm.

title: A death on the road
summary: Hidden. If the Master dies, the chain ends a month later (carnival.90 on the host). If the host dies while the Carnival is in their lands, the Master moves on (carnival.80 from the Master).

summary: Hidden. Five years after the Carnival reached a realm, if it has not moved since (a step that could not fire), it ends.

title: A cultist casts off the mask

title: The cult rises
summary: The cult leader proclaims their faith. They become a devout leader, break away from a top liege outside the cult with an independence war, and call on every cultist in that realm to rise too (chaoscult.1).

title: The truth revealed
summary: A revealed cult leader flips the provinces where their cult has a secret community to the open faith.

title: A vassal turns heretic

title: A cell is founded
summary: The cultist starts a cell in the target province. Diplomacy helps; a province outside the cultist's own demesne takes longer and goes worse. The outcome arrives after 300 (own) or 500 days: easy (chaoscult.16), going well (17) or struggling (18). chaoscult.14 watches the province meanwhile.

title: Watch the province
summary: Hidden, monthly. If the target province leaves the realm, the cell is lost (chaoscult.15).

title: The province is lost
summary: The cell cannot be kept up from abroad. The mission fails.

title: The faithful flock in
summary: The cell grows with ease and is founded in about 150 days (chaoscult.19).

title: The cell grows
summary: Good progress; the cell is founded later (chaoscult.19).

title: The cell struggles
summary: Pay to keep it going (founded after about 450 days, chaoscult.19) or give up and fail the mission.

title: The cell is founded
summary: The province gets a secret community of the cultist's god. Completes the mission.

title: Dinner with an open mind

title: Safety ping: no
summary: Hidden. Tells the recruiter (chaoscult.29), or chaoscult.32.

title: The recruit refused
summary: Notification.

title: The recruit said yes
summary: The recruiter picks a senior cultist as the inductor and confirms (chaoscult.31).

title: The promise
summary: The recruit hears what the god offers; forbidden study follows (chaoscult.33).

title: Contact lost
summary: The recruiter has died or turned away. Notification.

title: Forbidden books
summary: The recruit studies the occult and loses zealotry. The mark follows (chaoscult.34).

title: The mark in blood
summary: A mark of the god appears on the recruit's door. Carving it into the arm brings the inductor (chaoscult.35); refusing ends it (chaoscult.48 and a failure letter to the recruiter).

title: Find the inductor
summary: Hidden. Finds a free senior cultist if none is set and starts the letter step through chaoscult.36.

summary: Like chaoscult.150; minor or trivial.

title: Into the furnace
summary: A prisoner is thrown into Hashut's furnace. A Dawi of the Ancestor Gods is the prize offering, then a captive lord, then anyone else. Outside a grand rite each offering adds a point of Hashut's favour; in a grand rite Hashut answers.

title: The offering burns
summary: The offering dies in the molten metal. Its dynasty hates the sacrificer, and killing close kin makes the sacrificer a kinslayer. The truly undying cheat the furnace.

title: A prisoner is dragged to the furnace
summary: Hidden step that turns a chosen prisoner into the FROM of dawizharr.1.

title: The grand sacrifice
summary: The acolytes ready the ziggurat's furnaces. The ruler offers the slaves of a factory or of the levy pens (each costs a level of that building), or a prisoner. The rite costs 200 gold and Hashut will not hear another for about four years.

title: The slaves go into the fire
summary: Bull Centaurs herd a mass of slaves into the furnace. Feeds Hashut and draws his answer.

title: The furnaces are cold
summary: Four years without an offering. The ruler can give up a level of a slave building, drag a prisoner to the furnace, or let vassals and priests turn against them (must_sacrifice_hashut, lifted by the next sacrifice).

title: Hashut offers gifts
summary: The brazen idol speaks and offers a choice: K'daai to burn the ruler's foes, a body like a Bull Centaur's, Hashut's fire on the land, or (for a sorcerer) deeper mastery of the Winds.

title: A K'daai rises from the furnace
summary: A daemon of fire and iron climbs out of the molten pit and swears itself to the ruler.

title: Hashut sends a Great Taurus
summary: A Great Taurus, one of Hashut's favoured beasts, lands outside the temple. Never rolled for someone who already rides one.

title: Visions of glory
summary: The molten metal shows the ruler wealth and power. One time in four, if the ruler has none, a rune of Hashut's blood cools out of the metal (dawizharr_bloodhashut).

title: His greatest child
summary: Hashut's voice praises the ruler, who grows proud.

title: A crown of fire
summary: Hashut sends visions that burn the ruler's mind (lunacy, mutate.5).

title: A gush of molten metal
summary: The furnace spits in the ruler's face. Never rolled for the already disfigured.

title: Silence
summary: Hashut ignores the offering.

title: Bull Centaurs at the foot of the ziggurat
summary: A regiment of Bull Centaurs waits outside the temple to serve the ruler. (Restored from the old grand sacrifice results.)

title: Hashut's wrath
summary: A cloud of red smoke forces itself down the ruler's throat (hashut_curse for about four years). (Restored from the old grand sacrifice results.)

title: A Sorcerer-Prophet of Hashut
summary: Hashut grants a devoted servant mastery of the Winds of Magic. About one chance in four per five years, more for the pious.

title: The Sorcerer's Curse
summary: The sorcerer's flesh turns to black stone: first hands and feet, then the body (incapable), then the head, and the sorcerer joins the stone statues along the roads to Zharr-Naggrund. Sorcery cannot save a sorcerer from this last step. antideath_effect.

title: A K'daai is bound
summary: A daemon summoning ends with a K'daai Fireborn held in the circle.

title: A K'daai bound for another
summary: The sorcerer learns that the K'daai they summoned for their liege is bound.

title: Slave raid
summary: A Chaos Dwarf takes an enemy capital in a chaos_dwarf_slaver_raid war. The first such capital of the war fills a slave building at home; later ones only bring captives and plunder. Or the captives go into Hashut's furnaces. Up to five courtiers of the raided court are dragged off or burned. on_siege_over_winner.

title: Yearly upkeep of a Chaos Dwarf realm
summary: Hidden. Starts Hashut's seven-year sacrifice clock for a new ruler, asks for an overdue sacrifice (dawizharr.8) and herds slave buildings outside the capital to it (dawizharr.32).

title: The slaves are herded to the capital
summary: Slave buildings stand only in the capital. Those elsewhere (after the capital moved, or with a newly gained holding) are torn down, and each lost level adds a level at the capital.

title: The factory slaves die off
summary: Smoke, accidents and hunger thin the factory slaves: the factory loses a level (never below 1). About 1 in 26 per decade, far more often under a poor steward.

title: The levy slaves die off
summary: Brutal hobgoblin overseers and hunger thin the slave levy: it loses a level (never below 1). Same odds as dawizharr.33.

title: Fresh slaves arrive
summary: Slaves paid for an arms deal reach the capital: the ruler puts them in the factory or the levy pens.

title: Sold into slavery
summary: A prisoner is sold in the slave markets. The price follows their best skill. chaos_dwarf_sell_into_slavery.

title: The slave's fate
summary: The sold captive will be worked to death. Their kin hate the seller.

title: What will you buy?
summary: The buyer picks arms and armour or a battery of war machines (Hellcannons from the Dawi Zharr, cannons and Organ Guns from the Dawi). buy_from_chaos_dwarfs, buy_from_dwarfs and by dawizharr.45 and chaoshorde.21.

title: A buyer at the gates
summary: The seller hears the order. The AI always sells.

title: The price
summary: The buyer pays 150 gold, or (to the Dawi Zharr) chains up people of their capital, hands over slaves from their pits or gives up a prisoner.

title: Payment received
summary: The seller takes the gold, the slaves (put to work, dawizharr.35) or the prisoner, and ships the goods.

title: The goods arrive
summary: War machines come with a guard regiment and wait at the capital; arms and armour equip the capital's levies for ten years. A seller who likes the buyer (opinion 50+) may add a Hellforged Greatshield (1 in 4, once in the buyer's lifetime, dawizharr_greatshield).

title: A Chaos Dwarf offers wares
summary: Hidden step for the sell_stuff_chaos_dwarfs decision: hands the deal to the buyer as if they had asked.

title: The settlement grows
summary: Hidden. Rolls the next turn in the settlement's life. If the camp is held above baron rank (no chieftain to govern it) it is warned for two years and then abandoned (chaoshorde.9).

title: A settlement is founded
summary: The chieftain raises a tribal camp with its first buildings, and the settlement chain starts (chaoshorde.1).

title: The Wastes wreck a building
summary: The warping land destroys a building of the camp.

title: The settlement stands
summary: The camp has outlasted the Wastes: turn it into a city (trade) or a castle (war), with walls, barracks and a market or town. If the province already has both, the camp stays a camp.

title: Clansmen flock to the settlement
summary: Word of the camp spreads and warriors join the horde.

title: A young warrior raises a band
summary: A warrior of the camp gathers followers and rises in revolt.

title: The chieftain is murdered
summary: A champion of one of the gods kills the chieftain. The ruler can take the killer's oath and let them rule the camp, or have them put to death and leave the camp to the chieftain's heir.

title: The settlement is abandoned
summary: A camp without a chieftain to govern it (three years held above baron rank) falls to rubble and is torn down.

title: Karag Dum falls

title: The fate of Karag Dum
summary: A Chaos ruler who controls all of Karag Dum chooses: burn the hold and take it (A), hand it to a Dawi Zharr governor who sells its people as slaves (B), or burn it and leave it to four champions of the gods (C). Each god likes a different choice. Every power nearby hears of it (chaoshorde.22).

title: News of Karag Dum
summary: Rulers of the Old World, the Wastes, the dwarf holds and nearby greenskins hear that Karag Dum has fallen. Dwarfs swear a grudge against the conqueror and the Dawi Zharr governor; others may fear the conqueror.

title: A building burns in the siege
summary: Dispatcher: one building of the taken holding is lost (chaoshorde.37). Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The warriors run riot
summary: Dispatcher: a holding without buildings is razed (chaoshorde.33); one with buildings is sacked (chaoshorde.34). Strict orders spare an empty holding. Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The town is put to the torch
summary: Dispatcher for settled holdings (not tribal or nomad): an empty one is razed (chaoshorde.33), one with buildings burns (chaoshorde.35). Strict orders spare it. Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: Nothing left to occupy
summary: The holding is razed to the ground. The Dark Gods take note (doom), and the warriors may bring back a trophy (1 in 50, once in a lifetime).

title: The holding is sacked
summary: Notification: two buildings are lost and the holding is sacked for a year.

title: The town burns
summary: Notification: four buildings are lost and the holding burns (two years).

title: Your holding is ruined
summary: Notification for the owner of a sacked or razed holding.

title: A building burns
summary: Notification: one building of the taken holding is lost.

title: Orders for the captured towns
summary: The ruler tells the warriors how to treat the holdings they take for the next two years: lax, normal, strict, or no mercy (in a holy war, or for a zealous or wrathful ruler).

title: Slaughter
summary: Dispatcher under lax or no-mercy orders only: an empty holding is razed (chaoshorde.33), one with buildings is gutted (chaoshorde.40). Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The town is gutted
summary: Notification: eight buildings are lost and the holding burns (two years).

title: Razed to the ground
summary: Dispatcher under lax or no-mercy orders: any holding but a capital is razed (chaoshorde.33), buildings or not. Rare. Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The warlord binds a warband

title: The breakaway settles
summary: Hidden. After 50 days a breakaway warband can no longer be bound by its neighbours.

title: The kingdoms break away
summary: As chaoshorde.51, by kingdom: any province outside the capital's kingdom can break off, and the heir needs less prestige to hold the rest.

summary: The winner tells of the fight (one of eleven, from either side) and may carry a wound. The loser gets chaosfl.13.

title: Death in the pit
summary: The loser's last moments: they die by the winner's hand (unless invincible). The winner then faces the next challenger (chaosfl.14) or, if none is left, is crowned champion (chaosfl.15).

title: Who's next?
summary: The winner dedicates the blood to Khorne and calls out the next challenger (chaosfl.8).

title: Champion of the Blood God
summary: The last warrior standing: Khorne's favour, gold, prestige and piety, a warband for a ruler, half the time the Skull-Torc of the Pit, and a chance of a lasting blessing (chaosfl.20 to 23).

title: Called off
summary: Too few challengers came. Notification for the challengers who did, who lose Khorne's favour; cleanup follows (chaosfl.17).

title: Home from the plain
summary: Clears the tournament flags. Also sent to the host and every invited warrior 30 days after the call (from the decision).

title: Fearless
summary: The champion becomes brave, or sharper in war if already brave.

title: Hardened by blood
summary: The champion's body grows one step stronger (weak, fragile, soft, none, hardy, tough, strong), or sharper in war if already strong.

title: The red rage
summary: The champion becomes wroth, or sharper in war if already wroth.

title: Khorne watches
summary: Rare: +2 martial and +1 health.

summary: A Lord Magister (favouritism_colleges) offers to have a lesser member promoted for a favour. Accepting raises the member a rank and puts him in the patron's debt (or cancels a favour the patron owed him).

summary: A player Lord Magister whose wind already has a Patriarch, with every Patriarch's seat filled, may challenge him to a duel of spells before the Order. The challenge costs as much as the rank itself.

title: The duel is fought
summary: A duel of spells, not of swords: the odds follow the magic power, gift, learning and focus of both wizards, with the sitting Patriarch slightly favoured. The loser may be burned by a miscast.

title: The challenger wins
summary: The Patriarch steps down to Lord Magister and the challenger takes his seat. Once in a while the beaten wizard is burned by his own miscast.

title: The Patriarch wins
summary: The challenger is beaten before the Order. He keeps a little of the currency he spent and cannot challenge again for 600 days.

title: A Lord Magister challenges you
summary: An AI Lord Magister of the player Patriarch's wind demands a duel of spells for the seat (college_ai_challenge_effect). Accept the duel, step down, or spend college currency to have the challenge quashed.

title: Defending the seat
summary: The same duel of spells as college.51, seen from the Patriarch's side.

title: The Articles of Imperial Magic
summary: Announces a new college to the founder, his vassals and every player. The founder gets the legal-magic bloodline.

title: The college stores
summary: A trained member from Journeyman up (college_equipment_requisition) visits the stores and spends college currency on the tools of his art. Each item can be held once; better pieces need a higher rank.

title: Battle stores
summary: The Power Stone of the member's wind (one active at a time), staffs and rings of power by rank.

title: Robes and regalia
summary: Robes of the Order and warding amulets, better by rank, and the Patriarch's circlet for the heads of the Orders.

title: Study
summary: The grimoire of the member's own wind, from Magister up, and eyeglasses for close work.

summary: A landless Lord Magister or Patriarch (request_college_house) asks his liege to give his Order a house in the liege's capital. Granting it adds the local college building and wins the wizard's gratitude; Sigmarite zealots and lands where magic is outlawed are less willing. A refusal refunds the wizard.

summary: On the society bi-yearly pulse a trained college member may get one small flavour event: one for his own Order (Bright, Gold, Celestial) or the feast of the Orders, which anyone may get. About one member in eight per pulse, so roughly once in fifteen years each.

summary: A Bright wizard's experiment with Aqshy goes the way most of them do: loudly. Pay for the damage, blame the apprentice, or write it up as a success.

title: The feast of the Orders
summary: The college dines together and two Magisters of rival Orders start a quarrel across the table, with sparks. Take your Order's side, make the peace, or pocket the silver while everyone is watching the fight.

title: Death comes walking
summary: Hidden. Death comes in the guise of a pilgrim: for humans of the Old World faiths a grey-robed priest or priestess of Morr, for the Dawi a wandering priest of Gazul, for the elves a servant of Morai-Heg. One time in four, for every faith alike, it is no servant of death at all but a daemon of Chaos, come to play for the ruler's soul. More likely in old age, poor health and during the Nurgle plagues or the Red Pox. Once per life; never for the immortal, who have nothing left to wager. on_yearly_pulse random list.

title: The cats are blamed
summary: Since the epidemic came the town is full of cats, and the people are sure they spread it. The ruler can pay to have some examined.

summary: The liege will not spare the vassal's cats.

title: The talk of cats dies down
summary: The talk of cats dies down.

title: Witnesses come forward
summary: The ruler can set the investigator on the most likely witch, ask the court to watch, or accuse someone they dislike.

title: The most likely witch
summary: The accuser (the investigator or a courtier from blame.51) picks a suspect: a real Chaos cultist first, then a mutant or an unlicensed wizard, a rival of the ruler, a madman, someone of another faith, a wicked courtier, or anyone at all.

title: The accusation
summary: The accuser names the most likely witch and the ruler may imprison them.

title: Two rivals accuse each other
summary: Two rivals each say the other is a witch; the ruler picks one, both or neither.

title: The court points fingers
summary: Either two courtiers accuse each other, or a married courtier's new lover accuses the courtier's spouse.

title: A jealous lover accuses a spouse
summary: A jealous lover says a married courtier is a witch.

title: Whom to accuse
summary: The ruler names up to three courtiers they dislike.

title: A courtier may point out someone
The hunt ends
summary: After three hundred days the hunt is over: the accused are judged if there are any, else the ruler admits no witch was found.

title: The judgement
summary: The ruler burns the accused, lets them rot, or hands them to the priests. Burning a real cultist pleases the faithful; Old World zealots may come to serve (once in a life, 10%).

title: A relative is chosen
summary: The fear the hunt has stirred up claims one of the ruler's family.

title: The hunt has calmed the realm
summary: The hunt is over and the court is calm.

title: No witch was found
summary: A relative may still die at the hands of a frightened court.

title: A relative found dead
summary: A relative of the ruler is murdered as a witch.

title: The ruler is to blame
summary: The priests say the sickness is the ruler's fault for never going to the temple.

title: Back at the temple
summary: The ruler worships in the faith's own way and feels closer to their patron.

title: The double at the temple
summary: The spymaster's double calms the people for now. The ruse may hold or be found out, depending on the ruler's and the spymaster's intrigue.

title: A child for the temple
summary: A grateful family offers their zealous child as the ruler's servant.

title: The ruse is found out
summary: The people find out about the double and burn the temple.

title: The people are fooled
summary: The double fools the people and the unrest ends.

title: Vandals at the building site
summary: Two starving children are caught sabotaging the new temple. Mercy angers the workers; harshness hardens the ruler.

title: The temple is finished
summary: The temple is built if the capital still has room; else the builders took the money for another site and the treasurer gets some of it back.

title: The building is cursed
summary: An accident at the site; the workers walk off. If the ruler spared the children, one of them is hurt.

title: The dancing plague breaks out
summary: Tells the province's owner and every liege above them.

title: The dancing plague
summary: News of the dancing plague for the province's owner and lieges.

title: The music calls
summary: The ruler hears the music from the window. Joining in sends them to the street (or to the court physician first); refusing may not be enough if they have already caught it. Followers of Slaanesh hear the Dark Prince in it and may dance for him. sets got_dancing_plague if they caught it.

title: The court physician says rest
summary: The physician warns the ruler they will drop from exhaustion. Listening may be enough; ignoring them sends the ruler to the street.

title: Lord or Lady of the Dance
summary: The ruler dances with the people for a few hours and is loved for it. A follower of Slaanesh who danced for the Dark Prince wins his favour too.

title: Caught by the dance
summary: The character cannot stop. They may recover after a few months, get worse, or dance until a leg breaks.

title: The dance ends
summary: The character stops dancing and will not catch it again.

title: The dance gets worse
summary: The character can no longer eat or sleep. It ends after a few months.

title: A broken leg
summary: The character dances until a leg breaks and loses it.

title: A Great Plague breaks out
summary: The first outbreak of Nurgle's Rot or the Creeping Buboes since the last one ended is told to the owner, every player ruler near and far, and the owner's lieges.

summary: A distant player ruler hears rumours of a Great Plague.

title: Word of a plague nearby
summary: Refugees bring the tale of what the plague does.

title: The plague in a vassal's lands
summary: A player liege hears the plague is in a vassal's lands.

summary: When the Great Plague infects a province next to a player's lands, the player (and their player lieges) are warned once. on_province_infection of nurgles_rot and creeping_buboes.

title: The plague approaches
summary: Refugees flood across the border ahead of the plague.

title: A depopulated province recovers
summary: A province with no sickness slowly fills again. Capitals, ports, trade posts, good stewards, many holdings and hospitals help; war, sieges, winter and deep depopulation hold it back.

title: The Elder sings the ruler's praises
Praised by an Elder
summary: The wiser the Elder, the more the praise is worth.

title: Old wisdom
summary: The ruler may hear the customs of the forebears (culture tech), the lessons of rulers past (stewardship) or the old tales (learning). Rarely the Elder hands on their staff as well.

title: The Elders gather
summary: On a new game, tribal rulers of an Eldership people (the Ropsmann, Ancestor Worship faiths, the reformed Atruhayid), and any ruler whose title starts under Eldership, get the law and six Elders so the realm has electors.

title: The beloved judges the gift
summary: For months has drowned you in gifts: gems from Caledor, silks from the harbours of Lothern, little caskets of gold that arrive with every ship. All of it in...

title: The gift pleased
summary: The courtship score rises by what the gift was worth: magic 5, gold and seduction 4, poetry 3, power, hunting, revels and books 2, flowers 1.

title: The gift fell flat
summary: The courtship may cool. How likely, and by how much, depends on the gift: a failed show of power or seduction costs the most. At nothing the beloved is free to marry another.

title: A proposal to a courtier
summary: You barely know each other, yet has formally asked for your hand, in a matrilineal marriage.

title: The proposal goes to the liege (hidden)
The final word
summary: A ruler decides on their own proposal; a courtier's liege decides for them. (elfwed_propose_effect, elfwed.8).

title: The answer is yes
summary: The suitor gains prestige by the rank of the house married into.

title: The answer is no
summary: has refused. All the years of courtship have come to nothing.

title: An Asur wedding
summary: Elves from across the realm have come to your wedding. They congratulate you and your spouse, talk politics in the colonnades and listen to the music drifting...

title: A Druchii wedding
summary: The promise of life can only be bought with the certainty of death.Together you and your spouse raise the still-beating heart of the sacrifice to the shrine of...

title: An Asrai wedding
summary: There is a season for everything. In the spring of this cycle you are joined with your spouse, but as every Asrai knows, this season too will pass, and one day...

title: The courtship lapses (hidden)
summary: Each round of the courtship renews elfwed_courtship_alive. Once five years pass without one, the courting trait (which forbids marriage) is taken away.

title: Cast aside
summary: has decided to divorce you. One does not cast aside an Asur so lightly: as the wronged party, you may demand compensation in gold, or in land if has any to...

title: The spouse lets it go
summary: has let the divorce go through without asking for anything more than share of the costs.

title: The price of a divorce
summary: The higher the divorcer's rank, the more they pay. Refusing costs prestige by the spouse's rank.

title: The price is paid
summary: has given in to your demands. Once everything is signed and sealed, you are ready to say farewell to for good.

title: The price is refused
summary: The spouse may accept it, or contest the divorce and stay married.

title: Still married
summary: took your refusal badly and has had the divorce struck down entirely. It seems you will be married a while longer after all.

title: Land as the price of a divorce
summary: The divorcer gives up a county for every two they hold, at most three and never the capital, and a duchy if they hold three or more.

title: Remember a matrilineal marriage (hidden)
summary: A divorce ends the marriage, so whether it was matrilineal is kept as a flag in case the divorce is contested (elfwed.64).

title: Proclaim the claim?
summary: For six hundred years the Empire has had no crowned Emperor, only rival claimants and the Electors who will not choose between them. Now the nobles speak your...

title: The coronation
summary: The claimant is crowned, the old rival crowns are put aside and the Grand Theogonist gives him Ghal Maraz, taken from whoever holds it.

title: A new Emperor asks for the Elector's knee
summary: A herald stands in your hall with a letter under the seal of . has been crowned , writes, by the will of the people and the blessing of the cults, and the...

title: An Elector kneels
summary: The Elector puts aside any rival crown and brings his realm into the Empire.

title: The Elector's vassals grumble
summary: You have refused the false Emperor before your whole court. Not all your vassals were pleased to hear it. The softer-hearted among them say you have put your...

title: An Elector refuses
summary: The Emperor gains a claim on each of the Elector's Imperial crowns, his own and his kingly vassals'.

title: A pretender's heir inherits a weaker claim
summary: The strong claims of the claimants (history, a coronation by the head of a great cult) pass to the primary heir as a weak claim, which still makes claim_the_throne cheaper. A weak claim is not passed on again.

title: One faith triumphant
summary: The new Emperor mends the schism of 1359. One cult is set first among the great cults: Sigmar's, as in the lore. A player Emperor crowned by Ar-Ulric or the High Priest of Taal, or who keeps one of those faiths, raises that cult instead. The great cults may marry one another again, the feud ends for good (no peace of the cults is needed after it). The other cults keep their temples and their faithful, and no one is asked to convert.

title: The Grand Theogonist makes peace among the cults
summary: Once a game. The cults' faithful may marry one another again, the high priests debate their dogma, and every ruler of the cults hears of the peace.

title: The peace of the cults
summary: With a common foe at the gates, a claimant may also seek allies: a rival claimant, a Dawi king, or the King of Bretonnia. In peace, accepting costs piety and refusing earns it.

title: A plea for alliance against the common foe
summary: An envoy of has come to your court. The dead are on the march in the Empire, the envoy says, and if the Imperial lines break they will not stop at its borders....

title: An Arch-Lector dies
summary: His heir in the Arch-Lectory lays aside any witch hunter's vocation and is welcomed with piety. The Lector's title itself is given by the game to any Sigmarite theocrat who qualifies (title_lector).

title: A Lector takes an empty Arch-Lectory
summary: A new Lector who holds no Arch-Lectory takes the Arch-Lectory of Talabheim, or else of Nuln, if it has no holder or is only kept by the Grand Theogonist, with its temple barony.

title: The game start narratives
summary: Once a game, from the multiplayer host's start: the claimants to the Imperial throne are told of the Age of Three Emperors, and Valka the Serpent's tale begins (slaanesh.470).

title: The Imperial throne
summary: For a claimant player at the start. Westerland hears of Magritta's refused coronation as a wrong, the others as a wrong put right. Talabecland may set the claim aside for the war with the vampires.

title: An Elector crown or the Empire changes hands
The Reiksmarshal or the Emperor's Champion changes
summary: The Solland and Drakwald swords go to the new title holder, or back to the Emperor. Scope: any.

title: The Knights Griffon are founded
summary: The order is raised and a Grand Master chosen from the Knights Panther; every Sigmarite ruler of the Empire hears of it.

title: News of the Knights Griffon
summary: Riders bring word from . The Emperor has raised a new order of Templars from the finest Knights Panther, the Knights Griffon, sworn to guard the Temple of...

title: The Edict of the Wolf
summary: The clerk sets the old parchment before me. Its seal is the wolf of Ulric beside the arms of Talabecland, and its words are as hard as the day Ottilia wrote...

title: News of the Edict
summary: The sky over the city glowed red for three nights. On the orders of the temples of Sigmar were put to the torch, the priests dragged into the streets and the...

title: The Edict is read in your hall
summary: A herald of reads the Edict in my hall before my household and my priests. The cult of Sigmar is outlawed. I am to turn to and pull down the Hammer from my...

title: A year under the Edict: a preacher of Sigmar condemns it, and the
summary: refusers may rise.

title: The War of the Hammer
summary: The Sigmarite lords who refused the Edict of have raised their banners. They march under the Hammer and the twin-tailed comet, sworn to see the Edict torn...

title: The Edict is revoked
summary: The faithful of Sigmar have won. Under the Hammer and the comet they broke my armies and forced the Edict from my hand. The temples open again, and the priests...

title: The Edict passes to a new holder
summary: With the title comes the Edict of Ottilia, still in force. The priests of my faith expect me to keep it. The Sigmarite lords expect me to let it lapse, and...

title: The giver turns from the Wolf and the Huntsman: the Edict ends
News: the Edict is no more
summary: Word comes that Ottilia's Edict is ended. The cult of Sigmar may preach freely again, and the Hammer hangs once more above the altars where it was pulled down.

title: The Pantheon of the Old World
summary: After winning the War of the Hammer, the giver may raise a temple to the gods of the Old World in the capital and choose who it honours. Echoes the old Olympian temple dedication.

title: A title changes hands: are the seats the Emperor's? (hidden)
summary: Runs when the Empire itself or one of the three seat counties changes hands, and checks the Emperor.

title: The Great Cathedral of Altdorf
summary: The bells of the Great Cathedral of Sigmar ring out over Altdorf for a whole day. The Grand Theogonist himself meets me on the steps, Ghal Maraz's likeness...

title: The Arch-Lectory of Nuln
summary: In Nuln the Arch-Lector holds a great service of thanksgiving in the cathedral by the Reik, among the smoke of the foundries and the din of the Gunnery School....

title: The Arch-Lectory of Talabheim
summary: Talabheim lies within its great crater, the Eye of the Forest, and its Arch-Lector has long had to guard Sigmar's temples against the priests of Taal who were...

title: The Keeper of the Three Seats
summary: Once per game: the first Sigmarite Emperor to hold Altdorf, Nuln and Talabheim together. Every other Sigmarite ruler hears of it.

title: News: the Three Seats are one
summary: Word comes from the heart of the Empire: now holds Altdorf, Nuln and Talabheim together, and the Grand Theogonist and both Arch-Lectors have named the Keeper...

title: A young noble asks to study
summary: On the five-year pulse an AI noble may ask the parent he lives with to send him to the nearest open university. The bright, the eager and the diligent ask more often; heirs and daughters less often.

title: A child asks to study
summary: event_target:university the university.

title: Sent to a university (decision)
summary: From send_son_to_university. The parent picks the university.

title: Where shall the child study?
summary: Each university is offered to the lands it serves, while its city is open.
