Home a drunkard
summary: is home from the , and one look is enough. smells of the tavern, laughs too loud and calls for wine before noon. It makes you wonder how ever passed an...

title: Home better taught
summary: is home from the , and changed. is wiser, surer of own mind, and full of things you never knew. The masters taught well.

title: Home worn out
summary: is home from the with studies finished, but they have taken a great deal out of . Too many sleepless nights over the books have left grey and joyless.

title: Home married
summary: The student brings home a spouse, of the faiths and peoples of the student's own land.

title: Home ill
summary: is home from the , dragging feet. The cities are full of fevers and the students' lodgings are full of the cities' worst. will need to rest a long while.

title: Home a scholar
summary: Rarely the student brings home a thesis the masters thought worth binding: once in a lifetime, and only if he has none.

title: Home a hedonist
summary: is home from the . Having heard some of stories of wine, dice, duels and the daughters of innkeepers, you decide a student's life must be quite something.

title: Home a sorcerer of the flame
summary: An Arabyan student with magic in the blood learns the sorcery of Araby: an education trait a step higher, an Arabyan Scholar, a lore of magic and the power to use it.

title: Halfway through (dispatch)
summary: The student has done two years, which counts if he is called home early (university.25). Scope: ROOT is the student.

title: A letter from the university
summary: Each university writes of its own city. is the university.

title: Called home to rule
summary: A rider in your family's colours comes into the university courtyard with mud to the knees and a sealed letter. is yours now, and your people need their lord...

title: The Rectors take their chairs
summary: Once a game, from the multiplayer host's start.

title: A Rector dies
summary: A scholar of his faith and people is chosen and takes all his university chairs (university.32).

title: The new Rector takes the chair
summary: He takes the dead Rector's chairs and his students.

title: The Convoy's oath
summary: Once a game: the captain of the Erengrad Convoy swears to the ruler who holds Erengrad and joins their court as Convoy Master. The mercenary company becomes the city's own fleet.

title: Where shall the Convoy sail?
summary: Pick the port. Each market pays best for two of the five cargoes (erengrad_cargo_suits_port_trigger). Far ports pay more.

title: What shall the Convoy carry?
summary: Pick the cargo, then the Convoy sails (erengrad.12).

title: The Convoy sails
summary: Forty galleys put out from Erengrad. The player must put the Convoy Master in command and sail to the chosen port within three years. A blessing at the Temple of Manann (free while the temple is in the ruler's debt) makes storms kinder.

title: The Convoy makes port
summary: The Convoy Master has brought the fleet into the chosen port. The pay depends on the cargo suiting the market, the cargo's state and the distance; sometimes Erengrad booms, and rarely an Elven sea chart comes home. The ships are laid up and the Convoy Master comes home.

title: The Convoy at sea
summary: Hidden. Every thirty days while the Convoy is out: has the Convoy Master made port (erengrad.13)? After three years the run fails (erengrad.15).

title: The Convoy is lost
summary: Three years and no port, or no Convoy Master: the cargo rots and the ships come home empty.

title: The Convoy's season
summary: Hidden. Every five years an AI ruler with the Convoy and a Convoy Master sends it out without the sailing: gold, prestige and sometimes a trade boom.

title: The sponsor's share
summary: Two years after a Duma member sponsored a Convoy run: the share comes home, three times in four with a profit.

title: The guild master's ambition
summary: A rich guild master asks to be raised to the druzhina and seated in the Duma. Grant it (gold and a new Duma member; the boyars sulk), or refuse.

title: The burning warehouse
summary: Boyars' men burn a guild warehouse on the docks. Punish the boyars, pay the guild for the damage, or let it lie (and lose trade for years).

title: A guild's gift
summary: A guild leaves a purse and asks for a lighter harbour tax. Take it, or send it back.

title: Silver and old blood
summary: An old boyar house will marry its daughter to a guild master's son, if the ruler blesses it. Bless it (the city thrives), or forbid it.

title: The foundry burns
summary: A casting goes wrong in the Compound. Pay for the damage, or let the cannoneers sort it out themselves.

title: The man from Nuln
summary: A Nuln guild agent is caught copying the Compound's secrets. Hang him, ransom him back to Nuln, or let him go with a false copy.

title: The Dwarf engineer
summary: A Dwarf engineer offers to improve the Compound's guns, for a price. Pay (a ruler with an Erengrad battery gets a better one; rarely an engraved swivel gun for the treasury), or send him back to the mountains.

title: The Elven Quarter
summary: One of the largest Elven quarters in the Old World. An Asur mage asks to serve at court, or the traders offer an Ulthuan contract.

title: The foreign quarters
summary: Tilean, Bretonnian and Empire merchants quarrel over the best wharf. Favour one, and its homeland's ruler thinks better of you.

title: The Low City
summary: Refugees from the north crowd into the tents of the Low City. Let them stay (more money, more unrest and plague), or clear the tents.

title: The Temple of Manann
summary: The ship-shaped temple that floated free when the city burned asks for gold. Give (Manann's favour on the city: a free sea blessing for every Convoy run, a steadier garrison), or refuse.

title: Erengrad sacked
summary: Hidden. When Erengrad is won by war or usurpation, at most once in twenty years, the guilds flee to their manors and the city is sacked. The Duma or the holder can rebuild it (decision erengrad_rebuild, erengrad.51).

title: Erengrad rises
summary: The rebuilding is done with salvaged stone and traders' timber, and the guild district comes back faster than anyone hoped.

title: How big you grew
summary: An orc or goblin coming of age gets a size trait from martial skill: small below 10, average below 15, large below 25, huge from 25. Fired at 16, and every five years through greenskin.5 and greenskin.6 for greenskins created as adults.

title: Bigger after the fight
summary: A greenskin in battle grows one size step (up to huge). Brave, cruel and wroth greenskins grow faster.

title: Stomp da grot
summary: A goblin ruler catches a smaller grot pinching his grub. Stomping him makes the goblin one size bigger (and maybe cruel); letting him off does nothing. Rare: about once in 12 years.

title: Size catch-up for orcs
summary: Five-yearly check that sends adult orcs without a size trait to greenskin.1. Split from the goblin check so each has a cheap culture pre-trigger and orcs of any faith are covered.

title: Size catch-up for goblins
summary: Same as greenskin.5, for goblins.

title: Da Waaagh! in yer 'ead
summary: A landed greenskin of 30 or more who is pious (1000), a scholar, a mystic or a theocracy can take up the Lore of the Waaagh! Craven or content greenskins can only refuse. Theocracies may be refused by the gods (25%) or made full shamans (40%). Tells the father (greenskin.11) and the top liege (greenskin.12). One chance per character: refusing sets a flag.

title: Dat's my boy!
summary: The new shaman's father hears the news and gains prestige.

title: A shaman among the chiefs
summary: The top liege hears that a vassal has become a shaman.

title: A shaman joins the warband
summary: At war, an orc ruler of 20 or more can take in a young shaman as a son of the dynasty (older shamans for older warbosses), or refuse out of fear. At most once every ten years.

title: Da broken choppa
summary: An orc ruler at peace loses his best choppa to a clumsy grot. Rage (may turn cruel) or curse (may become stressed).

title: Da grot thief
summary: A goblin makes off with an orc ruler's choppa. Chase him (may turn cruel or wroth), let it go (may turn slothful), or, for cunning orcs, follow him to his stash (greenskin.22). About once in 15 years.

title: Da stash
summary: The thief's hoard: sell it for teef (may turn greedy) or arm the boyz (prestige, piety, may turn gregarious).

title: Fungus on da droppin' ground
summary: A goblin suggests an orc with stewardship 12 and no lifestyle trait grow fungus for beer. Plant fungus (greenskin.32, the gardener path) or plant the goblin (greenskin.31, the impaler path).

title: Goblin beer
summary: The planted goblin makes a nasty brew. Serve it (prestige, maybe a mushroom artifact) or keep "gardening" (greenskin.33).

title: Fungus beer
summary: The fungus brew wins over an upstart. Keep pouring (wealth, maybe a mushroom artifact) or try for fungus wine (greenskin.35).

title: Goblins on da lawn
summary: The planted goblins make bad beer but a fine display. Keep them (towards impaler, greenskin.34) or switch to fungus (mushroom artifact).

title: Heads on sticks
summary: No goblin steals any more. Become an impaler, or take a year-long impaler modifier.

title: Da best brewer in da camp
summary: The boyz love the fungus wine. Become a gardener, or take a year-long gardener modifier; both give a mushroom artifact.

title: Squigs in da cave
summary: A goblin ruler finds a squig nest in the caves under his hold. Herd them (greenskin.41 in about a year), eat them (prestige, may turn gluttonous) or leave them be. One chance per character; night goblins are three times as likely to get it.

title: Da squig pen
summary: The herd has grown and eaten two herders. Breed them bigger (stewardship and martial help; success leads to greenskin.42, failure ends the chain with a bitten ruler) or sell them to the boyz for teef.

title: Da great cave squig
summary: One squig grew into a great cave squig. Ride it (martial and the brave help: a great cave squig mount, a bounce into a wound, or maimed), or make it boss of the herd (greenskin_squig_herder for ten years, and the herd goes to war in greenskin.43 a few years later).

title: Squigs to war
summary: The herd boss has bred a whole herd. Loose it on the enemy (squig hoppers for five years) or hold a big squig feast (prestige, may turn gluttonous). Ends the chain.

title: Da boyz respekt ya more
summary: Greenskin Power rises one step. Needs piety 500 for step 1, 1000 for step 2, 4000 and martial 14 for step 3, 8000 for step 4. About once in two years while eligible; big, martial, gluttonous and generous warbosses get there faster.

title: Da boyz 'ave lost respekt
summary: A weak warboss whose piety drops below a quarter of the step he holds (250, 500, 1000, 2000) loses one step of Greenskin Power. About once in two years while it applies; small and timid warbosses lose it faster.

title: Zogged in da duel
summary: A greenskin ruler who loses a head-bashing duel and lives loses one step of Greenskin Power.

title: Gork or Mork?
summary: A greenskin picks Gork (brutal but kunnin') or Mork (kunnin' but brutal) as his patron.

title: A weak warboss (orcs)
summary: An orc ruler above duke tier who is unhealthy or not fighty enough and also has no prestige, low martial, or a crippling trait becomes a weak warboss. His vassals may press claims on his title (warboss.15).

title: Da boyz listen again (orcs)
summary: A weak orc warboss who is fighty again (more than 20) and healthy, at least four years after turning weak, stops being weak.

title: A weak warboss (goblins)
summary: As warboss.10, for goblin rulers, who need intrigue rather than martial.

title: Da gitz listen again (goblins)
summary: As warboss.11, for goblin rulers.

title: Too long at peace
summary: An orc ruler above count tier at peace and hardly fighty (under 5) becomes a weak warboss. About once in ten years.

title: Da big boyz want ya title
summary: The strongest greenskin lords in a new weak warboss's realm (combat rating above his) get pressed claims on his primary title. Once until he recovers.

title: Da boyz rise
summary: The boyz of a weak warboss above duke tier rise in a horde at his capital (warboss.50). About once in 40 years while he stays weak.

title: A Black Orc comes callin'
summary: A huge Black Orc turns up at the court of a weak warboss, or of a big realm (20 counties) with a sickly, puny or idle warboss, and challenges him to a deadly duel. About once in fifty years.

title: After the duel
summary: Clears the duel flags and the weak warboss modifier from both duellists.

title: Da runt wants ya job
summary: A greenskin vassal has challenged his liege to a duel for the leadership (duel_greenskin_liege_decision). Neither can escape it.

title: Da boss accepts
summary: The challenger hears that the boss will bash his head in.

title: Da horde falls apart
summary: When a tribal weak warboss above count tier dies, his king and emperor titles are destroyed and his vassals go free. Players nearby hear of it (warboss.31 to warboss.34).

title: Fall of a greenskin kingdom (bounce)
summary: Picks the players within diplomatic range of the dead king.

title: Fall of a greenskin kingdom
summary: Tells a player that a greenskin kingdom has fallen apart.

title: Collapse of a greenskin empire (bounce)
summary: As warboss.31, for an empire.

title: Collapse of a greenskin empire
summary: As warboss.32, for an empire.

title: Da big boss is dead
summary: When an independent greenskin king or emperor who was not weak dies, every vassal may break away (warboss.36). His prestige is split between the heir and the heir's siblings; a WAAAGH! leader's heir also faces the end of the WAAAGH! (waaagh.50, waaagh.51).

title: Break away?
summary: A vassal of a dead greenskin overlord can stay or go independent (to the next liege up if there is one) and keeps a claim on the overlord's titles.

title: A vassal breaks away
summary: Tells the top liege that a vassal broke away.

title: Killed by a greenskin
summary: When a greenskin ruler above count tier is killed by anyone but a count, a greenskin killer takes his title (warboss.42).

title: Killed by a greenskin count
summary: As warboss.40, for a killer of count tier and victims above baron tier.

title: You killed it, you bought it
summary: The killer takes the dead ruler's primary title (and a county if he had no land) and gains prestige. The dead ruler's liege is told (warboss.43).

title: A vassal killed
summary: Tells the liege that a greenskin took a vassal's title by killing him.

title: A greenskin horde rises
summary: Greenskins rise in a province with a troublesome greenskin population (or one marked for a horde). A leader is made by region (forest goblins in the great forests, night goblins in the mountains, savage orcs in the Southlands, orcs and goblins elsewhere), gets a temporary horde title and an army scaled to the garrison, and declares war on the owner's top liege.

title: Marauding greenskins
summary: A greenskin band appears in a wild province (wasteland, mountains, hills preferred) of a non-greenskin realm and rises as a horde (warboss.50). Not in Ulthuan, Lustria, Araby, Nehekhara and other places without greenskins.

title: Greenskins in our lands
summary: Tells the lieges of the province owner that greenskins have risen.

title: A troublesome greenskin population
summary: When a greenskin takes over land, every province in his realm held by a non-greenskin gets the troublesome greenskin population modifier and loses its greenskin settlement modifiers.

title: Greenskins back in charge
summary: When a greenskin takes over land, provinces held by greenskins lose the troublesome greenskin population modifier.

title: Settlers driven out
summary: When a non-greenskin takes a county that is not greenskin land, it loses its greenskin settlement modifiers. (Was a province event, which these character on_actions cannot fire.)

title: Da land iz green
summary: Make land green: the county moves a step towards greenskin land and the ruler gains prestige. The liege is told (warboss.64).

title: Da boyz settle in yer name
summary: Tells the liege that a vassal is turning land green.

title: Boyz from da new land
summary: Make land green: the county moves a step towards greenskin land and a band of boyz gathers there.

title: Greenskins settle
summary: Make land green: the county moves a step towards greenskin land.

title: Animosity
summary: Make land green fails: the greenskins fight each other. The ruler loses prestige and the county gets the animosity modifier.

title: Fund the expedition?
summary: The marshal asks for gold to clear greenskins out of a county. Hard in the Badlands and Darklands, in forests (forest goblins), mountains (night goblins), hills (hill goblins), jungles and against Black Orcs; easier with many commanders, big levies and a martial realm. Success (warboss.71) or failure (warboss.72) in about a month.

title: Da greenskins are gone
summary: The greenskin modifiers are removed and the land takes the cleanser's culture and religion (Tomb Kings, Jade vampires, Blood Dragons and witch hunters use a fitting local culture instead).

title: The greenskins hold
summary: The expedition fails. One time in ten (four in ten in the Badlands) the greenskins rise as a horde (warboss.50).

title: Syphilis
summary: An unchaste character, or one whose spouse is infected, catches syphilis. Only without the Reapers DLC, which has its own disease system.

title: Syphilis fades
summary: A syphilitic character in good health recovers. Only without Reapers.

title: Leprosy
summary: A character in poor health catches leprosy. With Reapers, the court physician is told and the leper's treatment chain starts.

title: Leprosy cured
summary: A leper in fair health pays a healer of Shallya 25 gold and is cured, unless supernatural events are off.

title: Lunacy
summary: A character slips into the first stage of lunacy (lunatic_1, counter 5). Fever, prison, paranoia, zeal and a coma that ends in madness each have their own text. The lunacy events in WHG_health_events.txt carry on from here.

title: Lunacy fades
summary: A twitchy lunatic in fair health, without a disease that rots the mind, comes back to their senses.

title: Possession
summary: Something takes hold of a character's soul. Followers of the gods of Araby blame a djinn. Daemons and mindless beings cannot be possessed. The voices (health.100 and 123) follow.

title: Possession ends
summary: The possessing spirit lets go. Every voice, omen and possession flag is cleared. Also fired by WHG_daemon_events.txt when a daemon is driven out.

title: Stress
summary: The weight of rule, council work or a regency wears a character down.

title: Stress eases
summary: A stressed character shakes it off, far sooner once they hold no office.

title: Depression
summary: A character sinks into gloom: orphans, cynics, the stressed, the sick and the ugly most of all.

title: Depression lifts
summary: The gloom passes, soonest for the content, the zealous and the diligent.

title: Falling ill
summary: The character catches a plain illness. Fired by health.14 without Reapers.

title: Illness strikes
summary: Hidden. A healthy character falls ill: a Reapers symptom, or health.13 without Reapers. Gloom, stress, a weak body and a damp cell make it likelier. Also fired by pregnancy and ancestor worship events.

title: Illness passes
summary: An ill character recovers, faster in a strong body. Also fired by the assassins events after a poisoning fails.

title: A sickly child grows strong
summary: A sickly child of two to seven outgrows it.

title: Pneumonia
summary: An ill character's illness settles in the lungs, most often in winter and on campaign. Only without Reapers.

title: Pneumonia clears
summary: Only without Reapers.

title: Lover's pox
summary: A bed partner has given the character lover's pox. Fired 15-20 days after a tryst by the seduction and harem effects, wol_seduction_events.txt and the mercenary decisions.

title: A wound heals
summary: A wounded character without an infection heals and keeps a scar. Rolled on the yearly pulse (health_wounds list) and fired by the wound treatment events.

title: The wound festers
summary: A wounded character's wound goes bad: an infection with Reapers, a plain illness without.

title: Infirmity
summary: Old age catches up with a mortal. Dwarfs are spared before 200 and elves before 500, and every long-lived or hardy race rolls far less often. Immortals, Chaos chosen and Grail Knights never grow infirm. Also fired by DR_misc_events.txt.

title: Incapacity
summary: An infirm or inbred mortal can no longer rule or think clearly.

title: Consumption passes
summary: A character recovers, sooner when young and strong.

title: Typhoid fever passes
summary: A character recovers, sooner when young and strong.

title: Typhus passes
summary: A character recovers, sooner when young and strong.

title: The plague passes
summary: A character recovers, sooner when young and strong.

title: Measles passes
summary: A character recovers, sooner when young and strong.

title: Smallpox passes
summary: A character recovers, sooner when young and strong.

title: The voice from on high
summary: A possessed character of a sane faith, other than a greenskin or a Chaos cultist, begins to hear a gentle voice. Pious and mystic souls hear it soonest. About once a century of possession.

title: Alms for the poor
summary: The voice bids the character give 50 gold to the poor.

title: The hair shirt
summary: The voice bids the character wear a hair shirt in penance. Courtiers find it unbecoming.

title: The twin-tailed omen
summary: A comet with two tails crosses the sky, and the voice says it is a sign meant for the character alone. Opens the omen events (118-122).

title: Put aside lust
summary: The voice shames a lustful character into restraint.

title: A chaste life
summary: The voice bids the character live chastely.

title: Put aside gluttony
summary: The voice shames a glutton into fasting.

title: Temperance
summary: The voice bids the character eat and drink sparingly.

title: Put aside greed
summary: The voice shames a greedy character.

title: Charity
summary: The voice bids the character give freely.

title: Put aside sloth
summary: The voice drives a slothful character out of bed.

title: Diligence
summary: The voice bids the character work without rest.

title: Put aside envy
summary: The voice shames an envious character.

title: Kindness
summary: The voice bids the character be kind.

title: Put aside wrath
summary: The voice calms a wrathful character.

title: Patience
summary: The voice bids the character wait on the gods.

title: Put aside pride
summary: The voice humbles a proud character.

title: Humility
summary: The voice bids the character kneel.

title: Scripture is wrong
summary: The voice says the priests have twisted the true faith. The character turns heretic. Only faiths that have a heresy.

title: The voice of battle
summary: The voice gives the character advice on war, and it is good advice.

title: The voice of battle falls silent
summary: The war advice stops.

title: Speaking in tongues
summary: The character babbles in a language no one knows, and envoys leave confused.

title: The tongues fall silent
summary: The character speaks plainly again.

title: The daemon's voice
summary: A possessed Chaos worshipper, a member of a Chaos cult, or a character with negative piety begins to hear a daemon. Cultists hear it soonest. About once a century of possession.

title: Khorne: the prisoner
summary: The daemon wants a prisoner to bleed. One of the character's prisoners loses health.

title: Khorne: mercy is weakness
summary: The daemon teaches that mercy is for the weak.

title: Tzeentch: secrets
summary: The daemon whispers the secrets of the court for a year.

title: Slaanesh: chastity is a cage
summary: The daemon mocks a chaste character until they give it up.

title: Slaanesh: lust
summary: The daemon fills the character's nights with longing.

title: Khorne: patience is cowardice
summary: The daemon goads a patient character.

title: Khorne: wrath
summary: The daemon stokes the character's anger.

title: Slaanesh: humility is a lie
summary: The daemon flatters a humble character.

title: Slaanesh: pride
summary: The daemon tells the character they are perfect.

title: Nurgle: temperance is joyless
summary: The daemon laughs at a temperate character.

title: Nurgle: gluttony
summary: The daemon is always hungry, and so is the character.

title: Tzeentch: charity is waste
summary: The daemon counts every coin a charitable character gives away.

title: Tzeentch: greed
summary: The daemon shows the character what gold can buy.

title: Tzeentch: kindness is a weakness
summary: The daemon shows a kind character how others use them.

title: Tzeentch: envy
summary: The daemon shows the character everything others have.

title: Nurgle: why strive?
summary: The daemon tells a diligent character that every labour rots in the end.

title: Nurgle: sloth
summary: The daemon lulls the character into idleness.

title: Slaanesh: desire knows no bounds
summary: The daemon teaches that all desire is worthy, and the character comes to desire their own sex.

calls: health.151; health.152; health.153; health.154; health.155; health.156; health.157; health.158
title: A new law
summary: A lunatic independent ruler has an idea for a law. Each choice tells the ruler and every vassal. About once in 35 years.

title: The turnip law (vassal)
summary: A vassal reads the liege's turnip law.

title: The breeches law (vassal)
summary: A vassal reads the liege's law against breeches.

title: The hole law (vassal)
summary: A vassal reads the liege's law that every subject must dig a hole.

title: The neighbour law (vassal)
summary: A vassal reads the liege's law that every subject must strike their neighbour once a day.

title: The turnip law (liege)
summary: The ruler hears how the turnip law is kept. Every vassal takes the opinion_insane_law penalty.

title: The breeches law (liege)
summary: As health.155, for the law against breeches.

title: The hole law (liege)
summary: As health.155, for the hole law.

title: The neighbour law (liege)
summary: As health.155, for the neighbour law.

title: The gopher maid
summary: A player lunatic appoints a gopher as their lady's maid and loses face. About once in 35 years.

title: Howling at the moons
summary: A player lunatic howls at the moons from the battlements. When Morrslieb is full (beastmen.85), the green moon answers. About once in 35 years.

title: The horse chancellor
summary: A lunatic ruler dismisses the chancellor and gives the seat to a horse. The chancellor is told (health.163). Only without the Zeus DLC, whose ze_lunatic.txt has a longer horse chancellor story. About once in 35 years.

title: Replaced by a horse
summary: The dismissed chancellor learns who took the seat. Also fired by ze_lunatic.txt and WHG_waaagh_events.txt.

title: Rats in the walls
summary: The lunatic hears scratching in the walls and talk of the Horned Rat, though everyone knows the ratmen are a tale. The dreams begin.

title: Something in the well
summary: A green light glows at the bottom of the castle well.

title: The barrow
summary: The lunatic digs into an old barrow and finds wet sand in a dead king's mouth.

title: The cats know
summary: The lunatic forbids the killing of cats, for the cats watch the sea.

title: A quiet village
summary: The lunatic rides to a fishing village on the Sea of Claws. The villagers stare and do not blink.

title: The tide rite
summary: The villagers chant on the shore at low tide. The lunatic learns the words.

title: The thing beneath
summary: Something rises from the sea. The lunatic walks into the water and is gone, or runs.

title: The longship
summary: The lunatic seizes a fishing longboat and rows at the thing with a harpoon.

title: Waking on the shore
summary: The lunatic wakes on the beach with a great tooth in hand. Either it was a fever dream, and the lunatic gains prestige and learning (or the scholar trait), or they slew the thing and keep the tooth (health_drowned_tooth) and the killed_an_old_one modifier.

title: The djinn lamp
summary: An old brass lamp in the treasury whispers at night of a city under the sand.

title: Black sand in the well
summary: The well brings up black sand, and the chapel bell rings by itself at night.

title: The Reman map
summary: A map in a dead tongue, bought from a scholar of Remas, shows a city in the Great Desert. It is not on any other map.

title: The weeping statue
summary: A statue of Myrmidia in the chapel weeps sand instead of tears.

title: The caravan
summary: The lunatic joins a caravan into the Great Desert.

title: The veiled oasis
summary: At an oasis no caravan master knows, veiled people sing the song from the dreams. The lunatic learns it.

title: The city of black glass
summary: The dunes slide away from a city of black glass, and something inside it opens its eyes. Walk into it and die, or run.

title: The sandstorm
summary: The lunatic steals a camel and rides into a sandstorm, the city's song howling behind.

title: Waking at the oasis
summary: The lunatic wakes at a well with a shard of black glass in hand. Either it was a fever dream (prestige and learning or the scholar trait), or they broke the city's heart and keep the shard (health_black_glass_shard) and the health_singing_city modifier.

title: The stars are wrong
summary: The lunatic notices that the stars over Lustria move in patterns, and the patterns are writing.

title: The skink at the gate
summary: A skink leaves a carved stone at the colony gate every night, each carved with the lunatic's face.

title: Temple gold
summary: Gold looted from a temple-city whispers in the strongroom.

title: Jungle fever
summary: A jungle fever brings dreams of a great toad-like sage on a golden throne, who already knows the lunatic's name.

title: Into the jungle
summary: The lunatic leads porters and a few mercenaries into the jungle.

title: The silent temple
summary: The jungle falls silent around a step-pyramid. Skinks watch from every ledge and do not attack. The lunatic reads the glyphs.

title: The dreamer
summary: Inside, a slann sits in a pool of starlight, and the lunatic understands that they have been a thought in its dream all along. Step into the light and be gone, or run.

title: The river
summary: The lunatic flees down the river on a stolen raft, pursued by something vast in the water.

title: Waking in the colony
summary: The lunatic wakes in the colony with a golden plaque. Either it was a fever dream (prestige and learning or the scholar trait), or they read the plaque and keep it (health_old_ones_plaque) and the health_dreamer_touched modifier.

title: Mittens
summary: A lunatic ruler with a pet cat brings it to the council. The spymaster blames it for a sneeze. Defend Mittens and the story goes on.

title: Sleepless Mittens
summary: Mittens wakes the ruler at night and leads them down a dark corridor.

title: Mittens the spymaster
summary: The spymaster lies dead, Mittens on their chest. The ruler appoints the cat spymaster. The council hears of it (health.183).

title: Mittens takes the seat
summary: Hidden. The other councillors hear of their new colleague (health.184). An immortal ruler may share their immortality with the cat (health.185).

title: A cat on the council
summary: A councillor despairs of the new spymaster.

title: Immortal Mittens
summary: An immortal lunatic ruler can give Mittens immortality too.

title: Lunacy umbrella
summary: Every two years a mortal lunatic or madness artifact wearer may suffer a lunacy event: a twitchy quirk, or for maniacs and raving lunatics without a madness the onset of one. Doom, Morrslieb, mutations, Chaos cults and cursed lands make it more likely; a madness artifact alone makes it less likely.

title: Whispers and shadows
summary: A twitchy lunatic hears whispers behind their back and may turn paranoid.

title: Unmoved by suffering
summary: A twitchy lunatic stops caring about the misery of others and may turn cruel.

title: Too stressed
summary: A stressed twitchy lunatic reaches for herbs to calm down and may trade the stress for an addiction.

title: Dangerous experiment
summary: A twitchy mage tries a reckless spell. Patience and greater power make success (lunacy.6) likelier than failure (lunacy.7) or disaster (lunacy.8).

title: The experiment succeeds
summary: The mage gains learning, and may keep their feverish notes: a library item that raises learning but carries the madness to whoever reads it.

title: The experiment fails
summary: A wasted night drives the mage a little further into madness.

title: The experiment goes up in flames
summary: The fire catches the mage: disfigured, or wounded or maimed if already disfigured. Drives them further into madness.

title: The drunkard feels poisoned
summary: A twitchy drunkard decides drink is poison and gives it up.

title: Blind Virtue
summary: A maniac decides there is no evil in the world. Nurgle, god of despair, scorns such hope.

title: Fake Mage
summary: A maniac without magic believes the Winds flow through them. Khorne, who loathes sorcery, despises it; Tzeentch is amused.

title: Despairing Laughter
summary: A maniac sees the whole world as a cruel joke and laughs at every misery.

title: Unfeeling
summary: A maniac stops feeling anything at all. Slaanesh, who craves sensation, despises the numbness.

title: Bloodthirsty
summary: A raving lunatic (or a maniac vampire) craves the moment of another's death. The Blood God approves.

title: God Delusion
summary: A raving lunatic ruler (or a maniac vampire ruler) comes to believe they are a god. Blasphemy under any faith that frowns on madness.

title: The bloodthirsty lunatic kills
summary: A bloodthirsty raving lunatic murders a courtier (lunacy_murder_victim_trigger) of the court they live in.

title: The victim dies
summary: The murder victim dies unless they cannot die. Their close kin, spouse and liege learn who did it (lunacy.18) and hate the murderer.

title: Murder notice
summary: A relative, spouse or liege of the victim learns of the senseless murder.

title: Killing spree
summary: A bloodthirsty raving ruler stalks their own lands for a week. One demesne province takes the bloodthirsty_rampage modifier for 800 days.

title: The mage blows up a building
summary: A bloodthirsty raving mage ruler destroys a building where they stand. The province's owner hears of it (lunacy.21).

title: Destruction notice
summary: The owner of the province learns that the mad mage blew up a building.

title: Nobody should be punished
summary: A maniac with Blind Virtue refuses to punish anyone and turns arbitrary.

title: No longer cruel
summary: A cruel maniac with Blind Virtue comes to pity their old victims and loses the cruel trait.

title: A prisoner set free
summary: A ruler with Blind Virtue visits the dungeon and frees a prisoner.

title: The fake mage becomes real
summary: A Fake Mage who has since gained true magic power sees the delusion fall away (nine times in ten per five years): the madness ends and the lunatic counter drops by 3.

title: The laboratory explodes
summary: A Fake Mage's potion blows up in their face and wounds them.

title: Mockery
summary: A maniac with Despairing Laughter spends a day mocking a courtier for their weakness (lunacy_mock_target_trigger). The victim is told (lunacy.28).

title: Mocked
summary: The courtier mocked by the maniac takes offence and may sink into depression. The maniac sees the result (lunacy.29).

title: Laughing at misery
summary: The maniac laughs at the courtier's misery and may turn cruel.

title: Nothing left to fear
summary: An Unfeeling maniac who is not yet brave stops feeling fear: loses craven, gains brave.

title: No more plots
summary: An Unfeeling paranoid maniac stops caring whether anyone plots against them and loses paranoid.

title: Cutting to feel
summary: An Unfeeling maniac cuts themselves to feel something: wounded, then maybe maimed, and a maimed one may end up incapable.

title: Worship me
summary: A ruler with the God Delusion demands worship: prestige, lost piety, and perhaps a statue of the living god for their court. Immortals do this more often.

title: Lord and Master
summary: A ruler with the God Delusion who is not yet of Chaos decides they need no other god. They can embrace it (and fall to Chaos Undivided, unless they serve the necromantic faiths) or cling to their faith while the delusion deepens. Only humans, dwarfs, elves, halflings and ogres are tempted.

title: No more love
summary: An Unfeeling maniac ends a love affair. The lover is told (lunacy.40).

title: No more hatred
summary: An Unfeeling maniac forgets a rivalry. The rival is told (lunacy.41).

title: No more friendship
summary: An Unfeeling maniac drops a friend. The friend is told (lunacy.42).

title: The lover is told
summary: The lover learns the maniac no longer loves anyone.

title: The rival is told
summary: The rival learns the maniac no longer cares about them.

title: The friend is told
summary: The friend learns the maniac has grown cold.

title: The weight of centuries
summary: An old vampire's mind frays: 7 in 10 times the lunatic counter rises (twice for Strigoi) and the lunacy stage is updated. Clever minds and wizards hold out longer; Strigoi and everchildren hardly at all. About once in 66 years, more often with great age.

calls: lunacy.14; lunacy.15; lunacy.2; lunacy.3; lunacy.5; lunacy.52; lunacy.53; lunacy.54
title: Vampire lunacy umbrella
summary: Every two years a mad vampire may suffer a twitchy quirk or, as a maniac or raving lunatic without a madness, catch one: Everchild Syndrome (everchildren only), Bloodthirsty, God Delusion, Exquisite Agonies or Heart of Melancholy. The bloodline, temperament and living family shift the odds; doom and cursed lands make madness likelier.

title: Everchild Syndrome
summary: A maniac everchild vampire stops fighting the child's body and becomes a child in mind as well.

title: Exquisite Agonies
summary: A raving vampire has felt everything the world can offer and hunts for any sensation at all.

title: Heart of Melancholy
summary: A raving vampire has outlived everyone and everything they cared for and sees no point in going on.

title: The everchild seeks its mother
summary: An everchild vampire with Everchild Syndrome runs to its living mother for comfort and blood (lunacy.61). About once in 33 years.

title: The mother is asked
summary: The mother decides: let the child drink from her wrist (lunacy.62) or push it away (lunacy.63). A mother who is an everchild herself plays with it instead (lunacy.64).

title: Drinking from mother
summary: The mother lets the everchild drink from her wrist until it sleeps. A mortal human mother can be turned into a vampire of the child's bloodline (lunacy_turn_mother_effect).

title: Pushed away
summary: The mother refused; the everchild sulks.

title: Two children at play
summary: A mother who is an everchild herself plays with her child all night. They become friends.

title: Partner of an everchild
summary: The lover or spouse of a vampire with Everchild Syndrome no longer knows how to be with them. A lover can end the affair; a spouse can stay for politics. The everchild is told (lunacy.66 or lunacy.67). Once per character.

title: No longer loved
summary: The everchild learns its partner cannot love a child.

title: A cold spouse
summary: The everchild's spouse keeps the marriage but avoids them.

title: A taste for excess
summary: A vampire with Exquisite Agonies throws themselves into excess and becomes a hedonist.

calls: lunacy.72; lunacy.73; lunacy.74; lunacy.75; lunacy.76; lunacy.77; lunacy.78; lunacy.79; lunacy.80; lunacy.81; lunacy.82
title: Something new
summary: A hedonist vampire with Exquisite Agonies picks a new way to feel something: pain (lunacy.72), feeding (lunacy.73-74), lust (lunacy.75-78) or the vampire's own banes (lunacy.79-82).

title: Cutting
summary: The vampire cuts their own flesh: wounded, maybe maimed, and a maimed one may end up disfigured.

title: Gorging on blood
summary: The vampire feeds on a dozen victims and feels nothing; may turn gluttonous.

title: Eating flesh
summary: The vampire eats the flesh of the living like a ghoul. Proud bloodlines at court are disgusted, and the madness deepens (less so for Strigoi, who are used to it).

title: Lusting after vampires
summary: The vampire takes eager thralls of their own kind to bed and feels nothing. May turn lustful.

title: Lusting after mortals
summary: The vampire beds a warm mortal servant and feels only thirst. Bloodlines that despise such appetites think less of them. May turn lustful.

title: Lusting after ghouls
summary: The vampire tries a ghoul and finds only stench. Most bloodlines are disgusted. May turn lustful.

title: Commanding the dead
summary: The vampire orders a corpse about to feel something new and finds it hollow. Costs prestige and piety. May turn lustful.

title: Daring the sun
summary: The vampire steps into sunlight for the thrill of it: loses health and has a 1 in 10 chance to burn to death.

title: Hooks and chains
summary: The vampire hangs from hooks for the strange feeling of flesh healing askew. Loses a little health.

title: Holy symbols
summary: The vampire grips the Comet and the Hammer of Sigmar to revel in the pain of Nagash's curse. Loses health.

title: Running water
summary: The vampire holds an arm in a river to watch it wither: loses health and has a 1 in 10 chance to die of it.

title: Nothing to live for
summary: A vampire with Heart of Melancholy sinks into depression.

title: Past glories
summary: A vampire with Heart of Melancholy dwells on better days and neglects the present. Loses prestige.

title: Into the long sleep
summary: A vampire with Heart of Melancholy withdraws into hibernation: gains the resting trait, and a ruler's capital takes hidden_hibernated_strigoi (vamp.60 clears it once they wake). Every few years they may wake (lunacy.88). About once in 30 years.

title: Stirring in the crypt
summary: The sleeping vampire may wake (losing resting and the capital modifier) or sleep on, gaining a little piety, and be asked again later.

title: The mind mends
summary: A sane character slowly sheds the strain that builds toward lunacy: the lunatic counter drops by 1. Without this the counter only ever grew, so a dwarf or elf living for centuries was all but sure to go mad. Long-lived and hardy races (lizardmen, greenskins) mend faster.

title: One-eyed
summary: Tells the character they lost an eye. and flavour events.

title: One-handed
summary: Tells the character they lost a hand. torture.

title: One-legged
summary: Tells the character they lost a leg. the dancing plague and others.

title: Starting fresh

title: A parrot

title: The cannibal feasts
summary: A mad cannibal eats a prisoner and takes in some of their traits and strength.

title: Eaten by a cannibal
summary: A close relative of the victim learns they were eaten. by the torture decision and Tamurkhan.

title: Disfigured

title: A golden mask

title: Scaring the children
summary: Hidden. The spouse brings up the children's fear (103). maimed.100.

title: The children are scared
summary: The spouse says the face scares the children. maimed.102.

title: A masquerade
summary: A masked ruler can hold a masquerade ball where everyone wears masks.

title: Invited to the masquerade
summary: A vassal is invited to the liege's masquerade.

title: A mad masquerade
summary: A lunatic host may decree that the masks must stay on for ever.

title: Masks for ever
summary: The mad host announces masks are now law.

title: The guests hear the decree
summary: The guests react to the mad law of masks.

title: Is the mad host alive?
summary: Hidden. Checks whether the mask law still stands.

title: The masks come off
summary: The mad host has died; the guests may take off their masks.

title: A fine masquerade
summary: The ball goes well and the host blends in.

title: The masquerade ends well
summary: A guest enjoyed the ball.

title: Masquerade cleanup
summary: Hidden. Clears attending_masquerade.

summary: Hidden. Picks a one-eyed event. list.

title: A thrown rock

title: Caught

title: Laughter
summary: The vassal is relieved the liege laughed.

summary: The vassal hears the bard was flogged and exiled.

title: Still singing
summary: The liege hears the bard still mocks him.

title: Roasted

title: The Black Boar
summary: The roasted bard is carried into the hall. Eat him and turn cannibal, or not. Piety is lost unless the faith is the Great Maw's or the Dark Gods'.

title: The palace holds
summary: Hidden. At the start of the game a ruler of Kislev who is no Ice Witch already pays the Sisterhood to keep the Ice Palace whole.

title: A new ruler of Kislev
summary: Hidden. The new Tzarina is crowned in the Ice Palace (tsar.3), the new Tzar at Ursun's temple (tsar.4). A ruler who is no Ice Witch finds the palace dripping (tsar.10); an Ice Witch stops a palace that was left to melt.

title: The Tzarina's crowning
summary: The new Tzarina is crowned in the Ice Palace with the frost crown, or in the Bokha Palace if the Ice Palace is gone.

title: The night in the bear cave
summary: The new Tzar spends a night in Ursun's cave before he is crowned at the temple. Go into the cave, or be crowned without it. Either way his reign begins with Ursun's Trial: he must win against Chaos, beasts or greenskins within five years (tsar.5, tsar.6).

title: Ursun's Trial passed
summary: The Tzar has won a battle against Chaos, beastmen, greenskins or the ratmen within five years of his crowning.

title: Ursun's Trial failed
summary: Five years and no victory: the boyars say Ursun has turned from the Tzar, and a pretender rises.

title: The Thaw
summary: The new ruler is no Ice Witch, and the Ice Palace drips. Beg the Sisterhood to hold it (a cost every year), move the court to the Bokha Palace and leave the Ice Palace to melt slowly (tsar.13), or let it melt now: a new age, an angry Ice Court, and a flood (tsar.11).

title: The flood
summary: The meltwater of the Ice Palace runs down the hill into the lower city of Kislev. Pay for the repairs, or let the city dig itself out.

title: The Ice Palace is gone
summary: Years after the court moved to the Bokha Palace, the last of the Ice Palace slides down the hill, and the lower city floods (tsar.11).

title: The Ice Palace rises
summary: An Ice Witch on the throne calls the Ice Palace back out of the frost (decision tsar_raise_ice_palace). Great prestige, and once in her life a shard of the Frozen Throne.

title: The Unwed Queen
summary: A great boyar presses his suit for the unwed Tzarina's hand. Marry him (he comes to her court, her house keeps the children), refuse him (he is shamed and may turn against her), or, as an Ice Witch, say she is wed to Kislev.

title: The consort's plot
summary: Very rare. The Tzarina's husband has been gathering boyars who would rather see a man rule in her name. Throw him in the cells, send him away to the frontier, or give him a seat at court and keep him close.

title: Heir of Miska
summary: A Tzarina who bears Fearfrost and throws back a Chaos invasion is named an heir of Khan-Queen Miska. The girls of her house are born with the frost in them more often (tsar.31).

title: Born with the frost
summary: Hidden. A Gospodar or Kislevite girl of a house with an Heir of Miska has a small chance to be born with the gift of ice magic.

title: The Tzar's Pulk
summary: The crown calls the Great Pulk (decision tsar_call_great_pulk). Send your rota (the crown's favour, Favour at Court for Duma members), or refuse (shame; a great boyar who refuses disgraces his house, tsar.43).

title: The Disgraced House
summary: A great boyar refused the Great Pulk. Shame his house before the court, call him out (the crown's champion fights him), or let it pass.

title: A guest seized
summary: Hidden. A guest under bread and salt is imprisoned by the host.

title: A guest slain
summary: Hidden. A guest under bread and salt is killed by the host.

title: Oathbreaker of the Salt
summary: The host broke guest right. Every Kislevite ruler hears of it.

title: The Ice Queen's Ball
summary: Once a decade the crown gives the Ice Queen's Ball. The boyars who come eat the crown's bread and salt (guest right, tsar.50) and something always happens among the dancers: a rival exposed (tsar.61), a marriage brokered (tsar.62), a witch revealed (tsar.63, tsar.64).

title: A rival unmasked
summary: Among the dancers a boyar is heard plotting against the crown. Seize him here (he is a guest under bread and salt), shame him before the court, or let it pass.

title: A match among the dancers
summary: One of the ruler's unwed children has danced all night with the child of a boyar. Bless the match, or forbid it. ruler's child, event_target:tsar_ball_match the boyar's child, event_target:tsar_ball_house the boyar.

title: A witch among the dancers
summary: A dancer is found with the marks of the Ruinous Powers on her. The Chekist takes her, or she burns before the court. witch.

title: The frost in her
summary: A girl of the court makes the candles freeze as she dances: she has the gift of ice. Send her to the Sisterhood, or keep her at court.

title: The Tzar(ina)'s Chekist
summary: Hidden. At the start of the game the ruler of Kislev has a Court Chekist: the Master of the Chekist at the Black Gate (73600, 2010 start) or a new one.

title: The Chekist's arrest
summary: The Court Chekist brings in the one the ruler ordered taken (decision chekist_arrest): a cultist, a mutant, a suspect, or a vassal who speaks against the crown. Taking a dissenter frightens the other vassals.

title: A boyar on the rack
summary: The Chekist has tortured a boyar who turned out to be innocent. Punish the Chekist, pay the family blood money, or say nothing (the vassals learn to fear the Chekist). event_target:chekist_victim the boyar.

title: The Chekist's own web
summary: The Chekist has been building a web of informers loyal only to him. Let him (a better network, but he grows dangerous), curb him, or dismiss him. A dangerous Chekist may turn on a ruler nobody fears (chekist.12).

title: The Chekist turns
summary: The Chekist with his own web moves against a ruler who is not feared. Strike first (one time in three he escapes to another court with his secrets), or buy him off.

title: A house for the Chekist
summary: Like the Order of Sigmar, the Chekist wants a castle of its own: a senior Chekist at court asks for a castle barony of the ruler's lands. Grant it (he becomes a vassal; Chekist standing), or refuse. Once in ten years. event_target:chekist_officer the Chekist.

title: The Sisterhood's missions
summary: Every two years each sister without a quest may be given one by a Grand Ice Witch: a proper focus, the hunt for a man who meddles with magic (Ice Maidens), or a new sister to find. The AI sometimes skips the mission and just gains or loses standing.

title: The hunt is ordered
summary: The Grand Ice Witch hands the hunt to the sister.

title: A man who meddles with magic
summary: Kislevite law gives the Winds of Magic to women. A man of the realm or a neighbouring Kislevite realm has been working magic; the sister is to hunt him down (the decision in wh_witch_decisions.txt starts the confrontation, kislev.7).

title: The confrontation
summary: The sister has found her quarry; the accused is confronted (gift.20 in WHG_magic_events.txt), and his lord decides his fate. The outcome comes back as kislev.8 or kislev.9.

title: Justice done
summary: The accused was burned or hollowed. The sister returns with honour.

title: The quarry spared
summary: The accused's lord showed him mercy. The Sisterhood is not pleased.

title: A girl with the gift
summary: The Sisterhood names a girl or woman with the gift who is not yet one of them: a player first, then the sister's own daughter, a woman of her realm, a girl of her Kislevite liege's realm, or of a neighbouring Kislevite realm (kislev_find_recruit_effect). The sister travels to meet her (kislev.12).

title: The sister arrives
summary: You have arrived at . Frost forms on the windows wherever sleeps, and the servants whisper about it. It is time to send for her.

title: The Sisterhood calls
summary: The girl may join and begin her studies (one to five years, quicker for the clever or those who already know Ice magic), or refuse if she is grown. Girls of Frosthome Lodge vassals move to the sister's court.

title: The girl accepts
summary: The sister starts her lessons (kislev.16).

title: The girl refuses
summary: has had the audacity to refuse you. The Sisterhood will not forget it.

title: The lessons
summary: Every year or so until her induction the sister chooses what to teach: caution, daring or focus (kislev.17 - 19). If the pupil dies or is already inducted, the lessons stop.

title: A lesson in caution
summary: Ice bites the careless. A rash or slow pupil has a small chance to die of the lesson; otherwise she gains Learning and Diplomacy, more surely with a teacher who has magic herself.

title: A lesson in daring
summary: The pupil is pushed to experiment. Timid or dull pupils risk the most; the rewards are broader.

title: A lesson in focus
summary: Discipline above all. Impatient, stubborn or wrathful pupils risk the most.

title: An Ice Witch
summary: The pupil's training is done. She becomes an Ice Witch, learns the Lore of Ice if she did not know it, and rises to the first rank. Her teacher hears of it (kislev.21).

title: A sister made
summary: The mission is done. Teacher and pupil may part as friends.

title: A proper focus
summary: A sister who wastes her days is told to give her life to study, the Tzarina's court, its secrets, or the defence of Kislev. Choosing that focus completes the mission (kislev.27).

title: The focus taken
summary: The sister has taken up the focus she was told to (on_focus_selected).

title: The Frosthome Lodge passes on
summary: When the Frosthome Lodge passes from an Ice Witch to a woman who is not one, the new mistress is made an Ice Witch of the second rank.

title: Rising in the Sisterhood
summary: Every five years an AI sister with enough Wintry Excellence may rise a rank (to Grand Ice Witch only if a place is free).

title: The call of the Legion
summary: Every five years a martial Kislevite courtier may ask their liege for leave to ride with the Gryphon Legion, Kislev's winged lancers (kislev.51).

title: To ride with the Gryphon Legion
summary: The liege may let the courtier go (kislev.52) or refuse (kislev.53).

title: Leave granted
summary: The courtier joins the Legion's captain. Years later they may come home a veteran, or fall (kislev.54).

title: Leave refused
summary: has refused you leave to join the Gryphon Legion. Others will ride beneath the feathered wings while you sit by the fire.

title: The Legion's veteran
summary: After years with the winged lancers, the legionary may come home with glory and skill, or stay with the Legion. One in eight fell in the Legion's charges instead; their old liege hears of it either way (kislev.55).

title: News from the Legion
summary: The old liege hears that their legionary has come home, or fell.

title: A child is born
summary: A ruler's newborn of Kislev's gods is commended to the gods: Gospodar and Kislevite parents pass the baby through Dazh's fire (kislev.61), Ungol parents call the Wise Woman to test it for Chaos taint (kislev.63).

title: Commended to Dazh
summary: Tradition calls for the baby to be passed through the ceremonial fire. Most babies cry, which is a good sign; some are scorched; very rarely one slips into the flames (likelier if the parents worship the Ruinous Powers or are mutants). Refusing costs piety.

title: Through the fire
summary: The outcome of the rite (kislev.61).

title: The Wise Woman comes
summary: Among the Ungols, a Wise Woman tests every newborn for Chaos taint (kislev.64). About one in twenty is found tainted, more often if the parents worship the Ruinous Powers or are mutants.

title: The Wise Woman's verdict
summary: A tainted child is taken away to be raised far from the stanitsa (banished from court); a parent who defies the Wise Woman keeps the child, at a price in piety and standing. A clean child carries one of the Hag's curses for life.

title: Fearfrost passes on
summary: Fearfrost, the Khan-Queen Miska's sword, goes from Tzarina to Tzarina. If its bearer dies and her heir is not a woman of Kislev's gods, the sword goes to the nearest such woman of her dynasty: a daughter, then a sister, then any kinswoman. The new bearer is told (kislev.71).

title: The Khan-Queen's sword
summary: Fearfrost has been passed down through the ages from Tzarina to Tzarina, mother to daughter, since the Khan-Queen Miska gave it to her daughter Shoika. In...

title: A sleepless night
summary: A restless Kislevite child wanders the castle at night (rare, from the adolescence pulse; curious and sly children are likelier).

title: The wardrobe
summary: In a forgotten room stands a wardrobe carved with frozen forests. The child may flee back to bed (kislev.102) or look closer (kislev.103).

title: Back to bed
summary: Without taking your eyes off the wardrobe, you back out of the room. Only when it is out of sight do you turn and run to your quarters, slam the door and leap...

title: Inside
summary: The wardrobe closes behind the child.

title: The frozen land
summary: The back of the wardrobe opens on a snowbound forest. The left path leads nowhere (kislev.105); the right to a ruined village (kislev.106).

title: The cold
summary: You follow the path for what seems like hours. Your fingers and toes go numb, and you begin to think longingly of the warm bed waiting in your room.

title: Something in the ruins
summary: A beast prowls the dead village. Running is safer (15% caught); hiding risks more (35% caught) but leads to the gem (kislev.109, 110).

title: Safe
summary: Without a moment's hesitation you turn and run for the wardrobe. When you are just a few feet away you glance back, but whatever it was has not followed you.

title: Caught
summary: The beast's claws find the child, who escapes bleeding.

title: Unseen
summary: You duck into the nearest doorway and crawl under the rotten frame of a bed. You wait without a sound for what feels like hours, until the presence fades away,...

title: The gem
summary: A gem of blue ice glows in the ruined hearth. Touching it awakens the child's gift: an Ice Witch for a girl, a warlock for a boy (and the Sisterhood hunts such men). A shard may come away in the child's hand (rare artifact kislev_wardrobe_shard).

title: Power
summary: As you lay your hand on the stone it flashes with a blinding blue light, and a cold power floods through you, sharp and wonderful. You cry out before you can...

title: Was it a dream?
summary: The child wakes on the floor in the morning sun; the wardrobe is gone.

title: One Kislev
summary: A Gospodar ruler who holds land in Kislev decides that Gospodar, Ungol and Ropsmann should become one people. The ruler takes up the new Kislevite culture and spreads it to Kislev city or one Gospodar province. Once per ruler; a player who refuses may be asked again. After that the culture spreads by kislev.151 - 153.

title: It's spreading
summary: The Kislevite culture spreads to one more of a Kislevite ruler's provinces in Kislev.

title: The new ways at court
summary: A courtier of a Kislevite ruler in the Tsardom takes up the new culture.

title: The new ways in the realm
summary: A vassal of a Kislevite ruler in the Tsardom takes up the new culture and is told so (kislev.154). Fixes the old version, which skipped the Tsar and every other independent ruler.

title: I am a Kislevite now
summary: The vassal's unlanded Kislevite courtiers follow them into the new culture.

title: Rebellious Erengrad
summary: At game start, a feudal ruler of Kislev who faces a burgher republic in Erengrad may claim the city by force (Kislevite and Norscan rulers call it tyranny) or demand a bribe (kislev.202). The AI ruler also founds the Tzar Guard five years later (kislev.205).

title: The fate of the Veche
summary: When the ruler of Kislev takes Erengrad after claiming it, they may burn the burghers' Veche and seize the city, or let the burghers keep their trade as vassals under the holder of the Erengrad duchy.

title: The ultimatum
summary: The burghers decide whether to pay the ruler of Kislev or defy them.

title: The burghers pay
summary: Erengrad pays and becomes a permanent tributary of Kislev.

title: Erengrad unmoved
summary: The burghers refuse. The ruler of Kislev gains a claim on the city.

title: The Tzar Guard
summary: The ruler of Kislev founds the palace guard (decision organize_kreml_guard, or five years after kislev.200 for the AI). A veteran captain is made its commander.

title: The guard reborn
summary: Notice for the ruler who founded the Kreml Guard (kislev.205).

title: Recruits for the Circle and the Duma
summary: Every five years an AI warrior of Ursun's faith may join the Circle of the Bear, and an AI Kislevite lord may take a seat in the Boyar Duma.

calls: kislevsoc.40; kislevsoc.41; kislevsoc.42; kislevsoc.50; kislevsoc.95; kislevsoc.96; kislevsoc.97
title: Society life
summary: Every two years a member may meet one of their society's flavour events, and a Grand Ice Witch is called to the Ice Palace.

title: The Bear Hunt
summary: The hunters have found the bear. Face it by Ursun's law (mostly the kill, kislevsoc.11; sometimes a mauling, kislevsoc.12), or lower the spear when it rises before you (kislevsoc.13).

title: The bear falls
summary: The kill. Counts for rank 2, earns Ursun's Favour, and may bring the Pelt of the Great Bear or, for a Champion, a bear too stubborn to die.

title: Mauled
summary: The bear wins this time. The hunter lives, barely.

title: The bear stands
summary: The hunter lowers the spear and the bear walks away. The priests call it a sign.

title: A Circle trial
summary: A Bear Brother chooses the trial for rank 3: ride north against a Chaos champion (kislevsoc.21), ride south with the Gryphon Legion (kislevsoc.22), or hold a stanitsa against the raiders (kislevsoc.24).

title: The champion of the north
summary: A Chaos champion has ridden out of the Wastes looking for a worthy foe. Fight him. Killing him wins the trial and pushes back the dark a little.

title: South with the Legion
summary: The Bear Brother rides south with the Gryphon Legion for a season of war in the Empire. They come home in a year and a half (kislevsoc.23).

title: Home from the Legion
summary: Three times in four the ride is a triumph and wins the trial.

title: The stanitsa on the steppe
summary: Raiders out of the north are riding on a stanitsa. Hold the walls, or ride out to meet them.

title: The trial is won
summary: Counts for rank 3. One time in four a bear-claw talisman comes with it.

title: The trial is lost
summary: The Bear Brother comes home wounded and must try again in a few years.

title: Waking Day
summary: Ursun wakes in spring and the host leads the feast: dance with the bear, bless the hunt, or judge the contest of strength.

title: A brother's pyre
summary: An old Bear Brother is burned on the steppe with his axe and his horse. Speak at the pyre, or sit with the old men and drink.

title: A young rider's challenge
summary: A young rider of the rota challenges the member to a wrestling bout in front of the Circle. Accept (mostly a win), or laugh it off.

title: The priest's escort
summary: The Rota of the Dawn guards a senior priest of Dazh on the road. Wolves, bandits or worse wait in the snow.

title: The palace weeps
summary: A Grand Ice Witch is called to keep the Ice Palace whole for the crown. Do the work (it costs her standing, wins the crown's thanks), or leave it dripping. A Tzarina who is herself an Ice Witch needs no help; a ruler who moved to the Bokha Palace or let it melt does not ask (tsar.10).

title: A task for the Duma
summary: A member takes on a task to rise in the Duma. One of four comes up: broker a marriage (kislevsoc.61), fund a rebuilding (kislevsoc.62), win a trade contract (kislevsoc.63) or speak at court (kislevsoc.64).

title: The two houses
summary: Two great boyar houses want a marriage and need a go-between who both trust. A diplomacy task.

title: Rebuild the burned town
summary: A town burned by raiders needs money to rise again. A stewardship task that costs gold up front.

title: The amber contract
summary: A southern merchant house wants a contract for amber and furs. Win it for the Duma. A stewardship task.

title: Speak for the Duma
summary: The member speaks for the Duma before the Tzar(ina). A diplomacy task; the crown's mood counts.

title: The task is done
summary: Counts towards the next rank. One time in six a Praag filigree chain or a sable kaftan comes with the thanks.

title: The task fails
summary: The bride ran away with a horse trader the night before the wedding. Both houses blame you.

title: A great feast
summary: The boyars come to eat, drink and hunt. Every Kislevite vassal and every Duma member of the same realm thinks better of the host.

title: A petition from the Duma
summary: A boyar of the Duma petitions the Tzar(ina): tax relief for their lands, or the crown's favour. Grant one or refuse (kislevsoc.81 tells them).

title: The crown's answer
summary: The crown has granted your petition: your lands are relieved of the crown's taxes for five years.

title: The Duma convenes
summary: The Voice of the Duma calls the boyars together. Squeeze them for a levy (gold, and some resent it), or let them air their grievances (goodwill and prestige).

title: Old blood, new blood
summary: An old boyar sneers at the druzhina as upstarts in borrowed furs. Side with the old families, or with the crown's new men.

title: Gospodar and Ungol
summary: A Gospodar boyar and an Ungol ataman quarrel over grazing rights at the member's court. Favour one or split the difference.

title: The guild master's gift
summary: An Erengrad guild master leaves a heavy purse and asks a favour of the Duma. Take it, or send it back.

title: The omens
summary: Once a game. The High Speaker of Ursun, or the First of the Circle of the Bear, sees the signs that the Father of Bears lies wounded in the east: a bear walks into the hall and lies down, the stars burn over the High Pass. Heed them and send a company east (ursun.2), or dismiss them.

title: The company rides east
summary: Choose who leads the company: the best rider of the Circle at court (or a champion found for the task), or the speaker in person.

title: The edge of the Wastes
summary: A Chaos warband crosses the company's trail. Fight (the leader's martial), or hide in the snow (the leader's intrigue). A loss counts against the quest; two losses or a dead leader end it in the Long Sleep (ursun.8).

title: The passes of the World's Edge
summary: Greenskins hold the pass. Fight through, or take the long way round over the ice (the leader's health and learning).

title: The Ogre road
summary: An Ogre tribe of the Mountains of Mourning blocks the road east. Pay their toll in gold, or fight. Then on to the resting place (ursun.6), or the Long Sleep (ursun.8) if the company is broken.

title: The resting place
summary: In a cave under the mountains the company finds a bear the size of a hill, breathing slow, with a black wound in its side. Offer blood (the leader's), offer a life (a prisoner), or take a tooth for a relic: the Tooth of Ursun, at the risk of waking the god in rage. Success brings Ursun Wakes to every lord of Kislev's gods; the relic gamble can bring the Long Sleep (ursun.8).

title: Ursun wakes
summary: Sent to every player lord of Kislev's gods when the quest succeeds: the Father of Bears is awake, and for twenty-five years the realm has Ursun Wakes (morale, piety, levies, a little health).

title: The Long Sleep
summary: The company is lost, or the god woke in pain and turned away. For twenty-five years Ursun sleeps: bears turn on men (ursun.9) and the cults of the Dark Gods grow bold in Kislev (doom rises a little).

title: Bears turn on men
summary: During the Long Sleep a bear comes out of the forest and mauls one of the court. Kill it (a hunt) or let the priests of Ursun try to soothe it.

title: The drunk boyar
summary: At the Waking Day feast a boyar, deep in his cups, mocks the Father of Bears in front of the whole court. Punish him, forgive him, or let him wrestle a bear and see what Ursun thinks.

title: The strongest man in the oblast
summary: A young man has won every contest of strength at Waking Day and asks to serve. Take him as a champion of the court, send him to the Circle of the Bear, or send him home with a purse.

title: Hidden. A siege takes the capital of a lord of Kislev's gods, and
summary: the temple flame of Dazh goes out (ursun.31 to the lord).

title: The flame goes out
summary: The capital has fallen to the enemy and the hearth of Dazh in the temple is cold. Until it is relit, the realm has Cold Hearths (fewer children, poorer health, no birth rites, no northern blood). Send a priest of the Rota of the Dawn to carry the flame back, make the pilgrimage to the temple in Kislev, or leave it for now (a decision relights it later).

title: The flame is lit again
summary: The flame comes home from the temple in Kislev, or in a priest's iron lantern, and the hearths of the realm are warm again.

title: Hidden. A war begins: a lord of Kislev's gods on either side may
summary: swear on Tor's thunder (ursun.41).

title: Tor's Oath
summary: The warriors gather before the war and the priest of Tor asks whether the lord will swear on the thunder: no flight and no surrender. One who keeps the oath to the end of the war gains martial; one who loses the war is struck down by the thunder (rarely) or is Oathless for life.

title: Hidden. The attacker won: the defender broke Tor's oath, the
summary: attacker kept it.

title: Hidden. The defender won: the attacker broke Tor's oath, the
summary: defender kept it.

title: Hidden. A white peace: neither side won, and the oath is simply
summary: released.

title: The oath is broken
summary: The war is lost. One time in twenty the thunder comes for the oath-breaker; otherwise they are Oathless for the rest of their life.

title: The oath is kept
summary: The war is won and the oath held. Tor's priests paint the lord's shield with lightning. Martial, once a lifetime as a lasting gain; after that, prestige.

title: The barrow of the Khan-Queen
summary: A Gospodar lord reaches the barrow of Miska on the steppe. Pray at the tomb (a chance of her vision: the Heir of Miska for a woman, Miska's favour for a man), or dig for the grave goods (gold and a curse). Grave robbers may already be at work (ursun.51).

title: Grave robbers
summary: The lord's guards catch men tunnelling into the barrow. Hang them, or take a share of what they found and let them go (gold and the curse).

title: The horse bones
summary: An Ungol lord of the old gods watches the wise women read the year in horse bones. Listen, or tell them to read it again.

title: The ancestors are hungry
summary: The spirits of the lord's ancestors come to the wise women and ask for a sacrifice: a horse, a prisoner, or nothing at all.

title: The dream of the bear
summary: Once the lord has read the bones or fed the ancestors, a great bear comes to them in a dream. Keep to the old ways, or turn to Ursun and the gods of Kislev. Ungols turn easily; this is the story of it.

title: The priests and the mutant
summary: A Kislevite of the court has mutated despite the northern blood, and the priests of Ursun demand they be cast out. Cast them out of the realm, throw them in the dungeon, or protect them and anger the priests. mutant.

title: The Great Warding
summary: A Grand Ice Witch goes to the Lynsk and pours her own life into the ice. For ten years her lord's provinces in Kislev are warded (no Spring Driving burns them so easily, and they are calmer), and doom falls back. The rite costs her health for the rest of her life. Once per witch.

title: The sorcerer's trail
summary: A Chaos sorcerer is hiding in the oblast: dead cattle with their eyes burned out, a village that dreams the same dream. Follow the trail to him (frostwitch.11), or send the Chekist and the lord's men instead.

title: The duel of ice and fire
summary: The witch meets the sorcerer in a burned village. A duel of magic: her learning and rank against his. A win brings currency, prestige and a little less doom; a loss brings wounds.

title: The frozen river
summary: The witch freezes the river in the pulk's path, and her lord's armies cross where no bridge stands (better organisation for a year).

title: The warp-breach
summary: Where the daemons came through in this war the air is still torn. Seal the breach (the witch's learning; doom falls a little), or leave it to the priests. A failed sealing costs her health or her mind.

title: The watch over the Ball
summary: An Ice Witch at the court of the Tzar(ina) keeps watch over the Ice Queen's Ball. Watch the masks (a cultist caught, her lord grateful), or dance.

title: A winter on the glacier
summary: A Grand Witch takes a novice up onto the Frosthome glacier for a winter. A test of the novice's health and learning: she comes down stronger in the Sisterhood, or wounded, or not at all.

title: Two Grand Witches
summary: Two Grand Ice Witches at the same court fall out over a novice or a seat at the lord's side. Settle it with a duel of ice (learning; the loser is wounded), make peace (friends), or yield the seat.

title: The hag of the village
summary: An Ice Witch meets an Ungol hag who calls the Sisterhood children playing with snow. Scorn her, learn the older magic from her, or, when Chaos is in the land, swear a pact with her against it.

title: The Sisterhood comes for the girl
summary: An Ice Witch has come to the hag's village to take a girl with the gift to the Sisterhood. Let her go (a better life, and the Sisterhood owes you), hide her and teach her the old ways yourself, or trade the old lore for the Sisterhood's respect.

title: The hut that walks
summary: An Ungol or Ropsmann pilgrim goes deep into the woods to find the hut of the Hag-Mother, the first of the hags, which walks on its own legs. Knock and go in (frostwitch.61), call her by the old name, or turn back.

title: The Hag-Mother
summary: Inside, the Hag-Mother sets her questions. A pilgrim who answers well comes home with her distaff (a great artifact, one in the world while it lasts); most come home wiser; some never come home. A hag, and one who called her by the old name, does better.

title: Return of the Chameleon Skinks
summary: Decade pulse when doom is high: Oxyotl returns and the Chameleon Skinks order is restored.

title: A blessed Skink
summary: Decade pulse: a Skink Priest is born from the realm's spawning pools (more likely when the court has few).

title: Skink succession
summary: on_death: hands the realm of a dead Skink ruler to his chosen heir or a gifted Skink.

title: Skink succession (ping)
summary: Hidden. Passes the succession to the new holder.

title: Skink succession (choose)
summary: Hidden. Picks the Skink heir: the title_skink_heir holder, or a Skink with magic.

title: Skink succession (inherit)
summary: Hidden. The chosen Skink takes the realm and treasury.

summary: Bi-yearly pulse: a sleeping Slann usually gains from contemplation; an awake one may suffer.

title: The soothing Great Plan
summary: Good contemplation: less stress, healing, patience or diligence.

title: The unravelling mind
summary: Bad contemplation: stress, sickness, sloth.

title: Realignment ultimatum
summary: From the faction_misaligned_chief_ultimatum decision: the faction demands the misaligned Skink chief step down.

title: Realignment refused
summary: The faction goes to war.

title: Realignment accepted

title: Realignment accepted (vassals)
summary: Tells the other player vassals.

title: Tlaqua restored

title: Lords of the Southlands
summary: Not fired yet (kept for a Southlands empire decision): the Southland kingdoms join e_southlands and ROOT takes the empire.

summary: Bones crack and stretch. Fur bursts through your skin, your jaw lengthens into a snout, and your screams turn into a bellow. When it is over, the thing in the...

title: Made a toad
summary: A ruler turned toad loses his lands a few months later (spell.55).

title: Made a pig
summary: A ruler turned pig loses his lands a few months later (spell.55).

title: The court is cowed
summary: Word of what the caster did to his prisoner frightens his court.

title: No lord for a beast
summary: A toad or a pig cannot rule; the transformed ruler gives up his lands.

title: The spell is resisted
summary: The target's own magic turns the spell aside. effects).

title: Humiliated
summary: Your spell slides off like rain off a roof. laughs in your face, and word of it is spreading.

title: The prisoner breaks free
summary: The prisoner turns the spell back on its caster and walks out of his cell.

title: The spell rebounds
summary: Your own spell rebounds on you. is free, and your face will never be the same.

title: Whispers in the mind
summary: The caster bends the target's feelings toward himself or against him for five years, unless the target resists (spell.60). (enfeebling_foe, lure_of_Chaos, mindfire, song_of_seduction).

title: The wood awakens
summary: The trees around the mage tear up their roots and march at his side. Only one wood may be awake at a time.

title: The forest sleeps
summary: The trees you awakened grow slow and still and put down roots once more. The forest sleeps, and you may wake it again.

title: The beast answers
summary: A great beast of the wild answers the mage's call and joins his court for a year or so.

title: Back to the wild (hidden)
summary: The summoned beast leaves; its summoner is told.

title: The beast is gone
summary: , the beast who answered your call, has slipped away into the wilds again.

title: The battle begins (hidden)
summary: The commander, and every casting flank commander of his realm in the same province, fills his magic pool and starts casting.

title: Casting (hidden)
summary: Every five days of battle the caster spends a point of his pool on spell units. The first time a player's mage casts, the player is told how battle magic works (battlemagic.5).

title: The battle is over (hidden)
summary: Checks every day until the caster is out of battle, then ends his casting and refills his pool for the next one.

title: Magic on the battlefield
summary: Tells a player that his commander has begun casting.

title: Battle magic
summary: Explains battle magic to a player, once.

title: Ready for war (hidden)
summary: Marks the characters who cast in battle and keeps their magic pool up to date for the trait text. A trained mage without a power level gets one. on_chronicle_start).
