title: The spells fade (hidden)
summary: Once none of his casters is still fighting, the ruler's spell units vanish. Spell units are always owned by a ruler: the caster or his liege. on_new_holder_inheritance).

title: On the march (hidden)
summary: A caster who enters a province or takes command starts the siege check (battlemagic.22) the next day. One who no longer casts loses the mark. on_command_sub_unit).

title: New ground (hidden)
summary: Entering a new province lifts the siege timer, so a new siege can start.

title: A siege may begin (hidden)
summary: Starts the monthly siege chain (battlemagic.23) for this province, unless one is already running here.

title: Siege magic (hidden)
summary: Each month the caster stays in a hostile province, from the second month on, he wears down its defences: a siege modifier as strong as his magic power (Khorne's summoners and the Red Duke count as power 2), at the cost of a point of his battle magic pool for three months.

title: Siege magic begins
summary: Tells a player that his commander has begun working magic on the walls.

title: Siege magic
summary: Explains siege magic to a player, once.

title: Nomad heir keeps the faith
summary: When a nomadic ruler dies, an heir of another religion group takes the ruler's faith. A government flip between chaos_horde_government and nomadic_government crashes the game, so the heir must match.

title: Samur chapter needs a witch hunter
summary: The Samur witch hunter chapter is destroyed when it passes to someone who is not a witch hunter.

title: The Everqueen dies
summary: A dying Everqueen hands Avelorn to her living heir (aiclean.4).

title: The new Everqueen
summary: The heir becomes Everqueen, drops her placeholder court title and receives every title of the late Everqueen.

title: Crown lost
summary: Every two years an Everqueen without Avelorn or a Phoenix King without Ulthuan loses the trait.

title: Dwarf newborns look young
summary: Newborn dwarfs and Chaos Dwarfs that inherited an old-age portrait set get the young one.

title: Growing old
summary: Every five years a human, Skaven or halfling of 50, or a dwarf or Chaos Dwarf of 200 (lifespan_age_50_trigger), gets the old-age trait that matches their looks; women become infertile and men less fertile, once. Old dwarfs get the grey-bearded portraits. Elves, immortals, Chaos champions and ice witches do not age this way.

title: Vassal conversion demanded
summary: Fired by the demand-conversion decisions: passes the demand to the vassal (aiclean.9).

title: Vassal conversion carried out
summary: Runs the vanilla conversion event 39700 for the saved converted target.

title: Spell failed
summary: Notification that a spell fizzled: the caster loses 25 prestige. Fired by the magic decisions.

title: Woodwalking ends
summary: Removes the woodwalking trait when its timer runs out. Fired by the magic decisions.

title: Greenskin government reset
summary: A new greenskin title holder on the second greenskin government goes back to the normal one.

title: Master dies
summary: When a mage dies, their apprentices are freed.

title: Dwarf ranks at game start
summary: Gives starting dwarf men the rank that fits their age and skills: beardling under 75, then thunderer, quarreller, hammerer or warrior, and longbeard from 250. Cowards are flagged and never become warriors.

title: Special titles die with their holder
summary: The Red Dukedom, Drachenfels and the Sylvanian empire are destroyed when their holder dies.

title: The Akghan church goes on
summary: When the head of the Akghan church dies, a new human mage of his faith and culture is created to take over (aiclean.17). The Rector of Martek is replaced by university.31.

title: Titles pass to the successor
summary: The new mage receives every title of the dead holder.

title: Elven youth
summary: Elves at adolescence become elven maidens or scions, which keeps them from low-born marriages; aiclean.19 ends it about 45 years later.

title: Elven youth ends
summary: Between 45 and 65 elves lose the youth trait, gain 50 prestige and can marry.

title: Court cleansing
summary: Every ten years an AI ruler below king with five or more Skaven breeders or ten or more Khemri soldiers at court quietly loses all of them. The AI spawns too many of them.

title: Mining outpost taken
summary: After a siege of a trade post, checks a day later (aiclean.22) whether the mining outpost still stands.

title: Mining outpost gone
summary: Clears the mining outpost flag from a province that lost its trade post.

title: Crown law cooldown cleared
summary: A new holder of a crown law title clears the crown_law_change flag.

title: Dynasty bloodlines
summary: A newborn joins every always_transfer bloodline their parents own when they share the dynasty.

title: Places of power and the Mists of Albion
summary: At the start of a new game sets the active, corrupt and inactive places of power across the map and the Mists of Albion (unless the game rule turns them off). Runs once, for the host.

title: Women's titles need a woman
summary: A man holding a female-led title (Sisters of Sigmar, Frosthome Lodge and the like) abdicates to a newly created woman of his faith and culture: a priestess for theocracies, a soldier otherwise. His court follows her, and the Frosthome heir becomes an ice witch.

title: Slann are Mage-Priests
summary: Gives every Slann the Mage-Priest character title.

title: Corsair titles
summary: Atruhayid feudal rulers with a port capital get corsair titles by tier.

title: The Dragon Emperor
summary: Fired from Xen-Huong's character history: creates the Heavenly Court, grants the imperial baronies and the nickname the Heavenly Master.

title: Game start setup
summary: At the start of a new game: Skaven surface tunnels under the burrows, secret faiths for members of the Chaos and Atharti cults, and male holders of female-led titles vanish (aiclean.26 has already replaced them).

title: Race trait check
summary: Gives a character without a racial trait the right one. Fired at startup, on employer change and by most effects that create characters.

title: Wrong faith
summary: A character in a faith their culture or race cannot hold is moved to the right one (by culture, liege and region). Players of human culture choose instead (aiclean.33). Gives up after 50 tries and logs the character.

title: Choose your faith, page 1
summary: The ruler designer asks a human player for their faith: the four Chaos gods, the necromantic faiths, Chaos Undivided, or the next page.

title: Choose your faith, page 2
summary: The faiths open to the player's culture: Norscan, Old World, Amazonian, Nehekharan, Cathayan or southern gods.

title: Choose your god
summary: The gods of the group picked on the first two pages.

title: Choose your vampire bloodline, page 1
summary: A ruler-designed vampire picks a bloodline: von Carstein, Lahmian or Blood Dragon, or more.

title: Choose your vampire bloodline, page 2
summary: Strigoi, Necrarch or Jade, or more.

title: Choose your vampire bloodline, page 3
summary: Mahtmasi, or back.

title: Choose your magic power
summary: A ruler-designed mage picks a magic power from 1 to 4 and, if untrained, gets a lore; then picks a potential (aiclean.40) if they have none.

title: Choose your magic potential
summary: Magic potential 1 to 4.

title: A lore for the untrained
summary: A ruler-designed mage who still has no lore or school gets a random lore.

title: Immortal portrait fix
summary: At adulthood an immortal race waits a month (aiclean.43).

title: Immortal portrait fix applied
summary: Sets the immortal's apparent age.

title: The Red Duke's bloodline
summary: At game start removes the Red Duke's bloodline from anyone but him.

title: Burnt by the flames
summary: A failed walk through the Flames of Asuryan founds the burnt bloodline, unless the redeemed one is already active. Fired by asur.3 and asur.4.

title: Redeemed by the flames
summary: A descendant of the burnt passes through the flames unharmed and is crowned: 500 prestige, 1000 piety and the redeemed bloodline for the whole living dynasty. Fired by the Phoenix King crowning.

title: Wonder levies refilled
summary: On loading a single player game, levies of wonder provinces at peace are refilled.

title: Move the Bretonnian court
summary: A new independent King of Bretonnia may move the capital to one of their own dukedoms.

title: Move the Imperial capital
summary: A new independent Emperor may move the capital to one of their own provinces.

title: Move the capital of Ulthuan
summary: A new independent Phoenix King may move the capital to one of their own kingdoms.

title: Wonder stage named
summary: Names and describes a wonder when a stage is finished. Not fired yet: most wonder names are still missing (was wh_setup.101).

title: Wonder upgrade named
summary: Names and describes a wonder when an upgrade is finished. Not fired yet (was wh_setup.102).

title: Seclusion ends with a new host
summary: A courtier who leaves a court in seclusion keeps the seclusion and food shortage modifiers forever unless they are cleared. (Was HFP.19000.) From on_employer_change and on_host_change.

title: The curse follows the ruler
summary: When a Mousillon county changes hands, every five years, and at startup: the holder gets or loses Cursed Mousillon on the Mousillon provinces they hold.

title: Startup: set the curse
summary: On startup the host runs mousillon.1 for the holders of the four counties.

title: The Red Pox returns
summary: Once a lifetime, a Mousillon lord finds the pox in the lower city. Shut the gates (mousillon.11 tells if it held), let it burn itself out (mousillon.12), or, for a master of the dead, let the dead rise.

title: Behind the gates
summary: Did the quarantine hold? Two times in three it did.

title: The pox burns out
summary: The pox has had its fill. A living lord who walked the streets may have caught it.

title: At Landuin's tomb
summary: A pilgrim (decision mousillon_landuin_pilgrimage) reaches the tomb. What answers depends on who kneels: a master of the dead faces the ghost (mousillon.23), the worthy are blessed (mousillon.21), the rest usually meet silence (mousillon.24), sometimes a curse (mousillon.22).

title: Landuin's blessing
summary: The worthy pilgrim sees the ghost raise his sword in salute.

title: Landuin turns away
summary: The unworthy pilgrim is shamed by the ghost and carries it home.

title: The ghost draws his sword
summary: A master of the dead at Landuin's tomb: the ghost rises to drive the thing out. Flee, or stand and fight.

title: Silence
summary: Nothing answers. The pilgrim goes home with the road behind them.

title: A cup of black iron
summary: Once a lifetime and only once a world: a beggar in Mousillon offers a cup of black iron that smells of blood. Drink (the Black Grail artifact, a dream in mousillon.31), refuse, or strike him down.

title: Dreams of the black cup
summary: The Black Grail speaks in its bearer's sleep. A living bearer may wake with a taste for flesh.

title: The last knight at the chapel
summary: Once a lifetime, the lord of Mousillon finds an old Grail Knight kneeling in the ruined Chapel of the Grail. Pay to reconsecrate it (mousillon.41 tells how it went), let him die there with honour, send him away, or, for a vampire, feed. old knight.

title: The chapel's fate
summary: The reconsecration took, two times in five. Otherwise the stones bled and the masons fled. The old knight dies either way, at peace or not. carries over from mousillon.40.

title: The Grismerie floods
summary: Once a lifetime the Grismerie goes under. Lead men into the water to pull out the drowning (a chance to meet the Dracoleech, mousillon.51), wait it out, or bind the drowned as servants.

title: The Dracoleech
summary: Something huge moves under the flood. Fight it, or get out of the water.

title: The bride in the garden
summary: Once a lifetime, a lord of Dras or a lord at court in Mousillon meets the ghost bride. Give her a courtier, wed her (unmarried only), call a priest (mousillon.61) or ignore her and be haunted.

title: The priest's work
summary: Half the time the bride is laid to rest. Otherwise she stays, and is angry.

title: The Mad Duke gives a feast
summary: Merovech (character flag mousillon_mad_duke, set in history) invites his vassals and a neighbour to dinner. Each guest gets mousillon.71.

title: An invitation from Merovech
summary: A guest at the Mad Duke's table, where the meat is not pork. Eat what is served, flee in the night, or poison the host (usually caught, mousillon.72; the host hears of it in mousillon.73).

title: Caught
summary: The poisoner is caught and dragged to the dungeons.

title: A poisoner at the table
summary: Merovech, a player, hears that a guest tried to poison him.

title: The Festival of the Damned
summary: Once a lifetime, the city takes to the streets in masks of the dead. Let it run (the taverns pay, the streets riot), crush it, or turn the mob on a rival at court (mousillon.81 tells the rival).

title: The mob at the door
summary: A rival hears who sent the mob to burn their house.

title: Mousillon under the dead
summary: The King of Bretonnia, living, sees Mousillon ruled by a vampire outside his realm. Once in fifty years at most he weighs a war (mousillon.91).

title: The Damned Duchy
summary: Call the knights of Bretonnia to retake Mousillon (claim and war on its vampire top liege, who hears of it in mousillon.92), or leave it to rot. Mousillon.

title: The knights are coming
summary: The vampire lord of Mousillon hears that Bretonnia has taken up the lance. A master of the dead can raise the duchy's dead to meet them.

title: The Black Knight rises
summary: Once a game, when the doom engine runs high or very high (the End Times are coming): the King's bastard Mallobaude appears in Mousillon with a pressed claim on Bretonnia. If a master of the dead holds Mousillon, Mallobaude goes to them (mousillon.103). Otherwise he raises a host of knights and Mousillon's dead and makes war for Mousillon. The King hears of his son (mousillon.101), the lord of Mousillon of the war (mousillon.102).

title: A son out of Mousillon
summary: The King hears that a black knight claims to be his son and his heir. Deny him, or admit that it might be so.

title: The Black Knight rides
summary: The living lord of Mousillon sees Mallobaude's host on the road.

title: The Black Knight kneels
summary: Mallobaude comes to the master of the dead who holds Mousillon and asks for an army. Back his claim (independent lords only), hand him to the King (mousillon.104), or drain him. event_target:mallo_king carry over from mousillon.100.

title: A gift from Mousillon
summary: The King receives his bastard in chains from the dead of Mousillon.

title: The Unliving offer their swords
summary: Once a lifetime, a herald from Mousillon comes to a necromantic lord at war. The Mousillonian Unliving (d_mousillonian_unliving) will march for gold: a host of dead men-at-arms that falls back into the earth when the war ends. Afterwards they can be hired like any company.

title: The touch of Chaos
summary: Every five years one character in five may face the winds of Chaos: one in five of those rolls the mutation toughness test, then may become a Chaos Spawn (mutate.2) or be forsaken by the gods (mutate.3). Higher Doom, the Chaos Wastes, warpstone, cursed Mousillon and the Geisterforst, magic and a Chaos faith make it likelier. Skaven, Kislevites, immortals and the Hollowed resist.

title: Chaos Spawn
summary: The mutations overwhelm the body and the character becomes a mindless Chaos Spawn. Also fired by the mutation table effects.

title: Forsaken
summary: The gods' gifts never came, only the voices: the character becomes Forsaken, loses any Chaos champion or chosen trait, and every friend, lover and spouse turns away.

title: A new mutation
summary: Notice that the mutation table has given the character a new mutation. Fired by mutation_toughness_test_effect.

title: The mind strains
summary: Something has strained the character's mind: seven times in ten (fewer for the clever, the magically strong and long-lived races; far fewer for lizardmen and greenskins) the lunatic_counter climbs by one and the lunacy trait follows it. Mutations make the strain worse.

title: Raving lunatic
summary: Notice: the lunatic_counter reached 20 and the character is now a raving lunatic. One in five finds an invisible friend. Fired by lunacy_counter_check_effect.

title: Maniac
summary: Notice: the lunatic_counter reached 10 and the character is now a maniac. Fired by lunacy_counter_check_effect.

title: Twitchy
summary: Notice: the lunatic_counter reached 5 and the character is now twitchy. Fired by lunacy_counter_check_effect.

title: Madness drifts
summary: Every five years a lunatic, or anyone whose counter has reached a stage, drifts: seven times in ten deeper into madness, three times in ten back towards sanity. Long-lived and hardy races mostly drift back, or they would all end up raving over the centuries. The counter is first synced to the trait so that treatments and vanilla events that add or cure lunacy are respected. Climbing a stage shows a notice; falling back is silent. Only characters whose counter has moved carry the lunacy_counter_active flag (set by lunacy_counter_check_effect); it is cleared once they are fully sane.

title: Serving a monster
summary: Every two years a vassal of a mutant liege, or of a maniac or raving liege, who is sane, unmutated and not of a Chaos or Skaven faith, comes to resent them. A mutant liege takes precedence over a mad one, and only faiths that frown on madness mind a mad liege.

title: The resentment fades
summary: Every two years a vassal holding mutate.10's resentment drops it if the liege is no longer a mutant or lunatic, or the vassal has become one, has turned to Chaos or the Horned Rat, or is incapable or trusting.

title: A mutant at court
summary: A witch hunter on a court hunt spots a courtier of their liege whose mutation shows (mutate_exposable_mutant_trigger) and confronts them (mutate.13). Order mission hunts use whunter.10 instead.

title: Discovered
summary: The witch hunter has seen the courtier's mutation. The mutant can beg the liege for mercy (mutate.14) or flee the court before the fires are lit.

title: The liege decides
summary: The mutant pleads innocence of Chaos. The liege can burn them, imprison them, or spare them (whunter.17-19). Burning or imprisoning upholds the hunter's accusation.

title: Exposed
summary: Every year a follower of an Old World faith whose mutations can no longer be hidden (major or massive; minor for the AI), who is not hiding and lacks the cunning (intrigue 12) to keep them covered, is seen and cut down by their own court. Players in the realm hear of a landed victim (mutate.16).

title: A lord cut down
summary: Players hear that a fellow lord of the realm was cut down by their own guards as a mutant. They can choose not to hear such news again.

title: Storm
summary: A storm falls on the fleet; worse in the Sea of Claws. Ride it out, pray to Manann, or run for the coast and lose time.

title: Man overboard
summary: A sailor goes over the side in a heavy sea. Go in after him, throw a line, or leave him to Manann.

title: Sickness aboard
summary: A fever runs through the crews. Put in at the nearest port and lose time, or press on and risk it.

title: Longships!
summary: Norscan raiders come out of the sea-mist. Fight, pay them off, or try to outrun them.

title: The Norscan toll
summary: A jarl's longships bar the strait and demand a toll. Pay, refuse (the raiders come, naval.11), or, if the commander's lord rules, swear a trade-friendship that opens a route north.

title: Something in the water
summary: A sea monster is sighted in the Sea of Claws. Hunt it (naval.13), or steer clear.

title: On its trail
summary: Days of following wreckage and blood in the water. Press on (naval.14), or give up the hunt.

title: The leviathan rises
summary: The monster turns on the hunters. Win (naval.15) or lose (naval.16).

title: The leviathan dies
summary: The hunters bring back its tooth: half the time the commander keeps one, once a lifetime.

title: The leviathan wins
summary: Ships are lost, the commander is hurt, and the beast swims free.

title: A pirate's offer
summary: A pirate captain offers to sail under the commander's lord's flag in return for amnesty. Accept (the top liege gets his ships; in some years the pirate may turn, naval.18), refuse, or hang him.

title: The pirate's choice
summary: Years later the pardoned pirate keeps faith (two times in three) or sails off with the ships and a hold full of the realm's silver.

title: Elven sails
summary: An Asur trading ship hails the fleet. Trade, or let an Elf mage take passage. The Erengrad Convoy Master can win an Ulthuan trade deal for Erengrad instead.

title: The White Star
summary: The Knights of the White Star, Ulric's knights of Erengrad, offer their warships as escort through the Sea of Claws. Raiders and tolls keep away for a year; the Orthodoxy of Ursun dislikes the favour to Ulric.

title: Hostile fleet nearby

title: The Frost Fair
summary: In a hard winter the rivers of Kislev freeze and a fair grows on the ice. Walk the fair (one of oblast.2 - 5), or stay in the warm. The ice may crack under the crowd (oblast.6).

title: The race on the ice
summary: Horses race on the frozen river. Bet on the Ungol mare, on the Gospodar stallion, or keep your purse shut.

title: The bear pit
summary: Showmen have dug a pit in the ice and set dogs on a chained bear. The crowd loves it; the priests of Ursun do not.

title: The Praag jeweller
summary: A silversmith from Praag sells filigree on the ice. Buy a chain (once a lifetime, only for one without), or haggle and walk away.

title: The cutpurse
summary: A cutpurse caught with his hand in the lord's purse has a Chaos mark under his shirt. Hand him to the priests (piety), or have him followed to his masters (intrigue, and a cult broken or a scout lost).

title: The ice cracks
summary: The river ice gives way under the crowd. Go in after the drowning (a chance of a wound and great prestige), or watch from the bank and lose a courtier to the river.

title: The Long Ride
summary: Every ten years the Ungol tribes hold a great horse race across the steppe. Ride in it (oblast.11), stake a horse, place a bet, or watch.

title: The ride
summary: The race runs from dawn to dusk across the steppe. A win brings great prestige and, rarely, a famous steppe horse (once a lifetime, only for a rider without one). A Gospodar winner galls the Ungols. A bad fall brings a wound.

title: The cub
summary: Hunters bring in a bear cub whose mother they killed. Keep it (a cub that grows into a companion in five to eight years, oblast.21), give it to the priests of Ursun, or let the hunters have the pelt.

title: The cub is grown
summary: The cub is a full-grown bear that follows its master like a dog. Keep it as a companion (a trait), or, for a member of the Circle of the Bear, train it for war (the war bear mount). It dies of age in time (oblast.25).

title: The bear is sick
summary: The companion bear will not eat. Pay a Strigany animal healer, or leave it to Ursun (it may die, oblast.25).

title: The bear mauls a guest
summary: A guest teased the companion bear and lost half an arm. Pay the guest's family, or say he had it coming.

title: The bear and the assassin
summary: A knife in the dark, and the companion bear gets to the assassin first. Once a lifetime.

title: The old bear dies
summary: The companion bear dies of age or sickness, and its master grieves.

title: The drinking contest
summary: A rival or a boyar challenges the lord to drink him under the table. Accept (a contest of health and martial, oblast.31), or decline and be mocked.

title: Under the table
summary: Who falls first? A win brings a bet and, from a rival, sometimes a sworn friendship; a loss spills a secret or costs a wager. Rarely, the loser wakes to find he signed away a hunting lodge.

title: Blood feud
summary: Two of the lord's vassals have fallen into a blood feud over a stolen bride, a dead horse or an insult at the bear dance. Rule for one (his loyalty, the other's grudge), share the blame, or let them fight it out (oblast.41).

title: Burnt farms
summary: The feud that nobody stopped has burned half a district. The lord's capital county has more unrest for five years, and the two families hate each other.

title: A letter from the Legion
summary: Kin who ride with the Gryphon Legion in the Empire (kislev.50 - 55) write home of a battle, and send loot.

title: A southern wife
summary: The kin in the Legion writes that he has married an Imperial widow. Bless the match, or forbid it and anger him.

title: A debt in Nuln
summary: The kin in the Legion has run up a gambling debt in Nuln and begs for gold. Pay it, or let him find his own way out.

title: The ataman's choosing
summary: Once per ruler: an ageing Ungol lord's stanitsa wants to know which son will lead it. Choose by election, by duel, or by the bear-wrestling. The winner is the stanitsa's favoured heir; his brothers resent it. Rarely an Ungol horn bow for him. event_target:stanitsa_ataman the chosen son.

title: An Ungol asks for the druzhina
summary: An Ungol vassal asks a Gospodar or Kislevite lord to be raised to the druzhina and seated in the Boyar Duma. Raise him (the Gospodar boyars resent it), or refuse (the Ungols resent that). the vassal.

title: The wise woman
summary: An old Ungol wise woman, a hag of the steppe, comes to court. Take her in (a hag-witch courtier), ask her to read the omens, or drive her off (she may lay the Hag's mark on the ruler). Ungol or Ropsmann capital.

title: The High Speaker's priests
summary: Priests of Ursun come to an Ungol lord of the northern gods whose liege keeps Kislev's gods. Take up the faith of Ursun, Dazh and Tor (the liege is pleased), or keep the old gods. kislev_gods.

title: The spirits of the wood
summary: Priests of Ursun come to a Ropsmann lord of the northern gods. The Ropsmann rarely listen: take up the new faith, or send the priests back with the old answer. kislev_gods.

title: A stanitsa turns to Ursun
summary: Every five years: one Ungol stanitsa of the northern gods in a ruler's lands takes up Kislev's gods by itself. The Ropsmann never do.

title: The mission to the stanitsas
summary: A ruler of Kislev's gods sends a mission to a stanitsa of the northern gods. The Orthodoxy's way is sermon and sword (piety); the Ice Court's way is druzhina titles and trade (gold). Ungols mostly turn; the Ropsmann mostly don't, and resent being asked.

title: The stanitsa refuses
summary: The mission fails; the stanitsa is angry for years.

title: The stanitsa turns
summary: The mission succeeds: the stanitsa keeps Ursun, Dazh and Tor now.

title: The last stand
summary: Ungol raiders fall on a Ropsmann camp. Stand with the pikes (a fight the Ropsmann know how to win), fall back into the woods (the camp burns), or pay them off.

title: Furs and amber
summary: Gospodar merchants come for the Ropsmann's furs and amber. Sell to them (a few years of good trade), take the amber to Erengrad yourself, or keep outsiders away from the camps.

title: One people, or our own
summary: Once per ruler: the Kislevite ways are spreading. Become Kislevite (the ruler and their Ropsmann court take up the new culture), or stay apart (the ruler's Ropsmann lands and court hold out against the melting pot).

title: The keeper of the tongue
summary: Rarely, an old keeper of the Ropsmann tongue, the speech Kislevarin came from, comes to a court with Ropsmann lands. Take them in (learning at court; the court's Ropsmann hold out against the melting pot; one time in ten a birch-bark chronicle), or send them away.

title: A pilgrim arrested
summary: Hidden. A pilgrim who is imprisoned stops the pilgrimage (clears the pilgrimage flags and trait).

title: A stolen spouse comes home (victory)
summary: Hidden. When a war ends, a spouse the defender took as a consort from the attacker goes back. on_war_ended_victory.

title: A stolen spouse comes home (defeat)
summary: Hidden. When a war ends, a spouse the attacker took as a consort from the defender goes back. on_war_ended_defeat.

title: Praag falls
summary: Hidden. A servant of Chaos wins a siege of a Praag holding: the city has fallen. If the curse was eased, it comes back at once.

title: Praag changes hands
summary: Hidden. A servant of Chaos taking the county counts as the fall. A free ruler taking it after the fall brings down the curse (praag.3).

title: The Curse of Praag
summary: The city is free again, but what the Chaos sorcerers did to it does not leave. Faces in the walls, madness, and the richest craftsmen in Kislev.

title: The curse returns
summary: Hidden. Every five years: when the Duma's rebuilding has worn off, the curse comes back.

title: The city takes another mind
summary: A courtier who lives in cursed Praag begins to hear the walls. Send them to the Ice Witches for healing, or let it run its course.

title: A child of the walls
summary: A child is born with the mark of the curse on them. Hide them, send them to the Ice Witches, or give them to the Furnace.

title: Faces in the walls
summary: Agonised faces push out of the stones of the palace. Pray, wall them over, or listen to what they say (a secret, and a step towards madness).

title: The Furnace men
summary: The men who smash the risen dead at night ask for gold, oil and men. Help them (Ashes Not Graves on the city; rarely their hammer for the ruler), or send them away.

title: The dead walk in Praag
summary: A district wakes to find its dead walking. Likelier when the Furnace men were sent away. Lead the Furnace men yourself, pay the garrison, or close the district and let it burn.

title: The undertaker
summary: One of Praag's undertakers is found raising what he should be burning. Burn him, take him into service, or drive him out.

title: The silversmiths' street
summary: The jewellers of Praag offer a commission. Pay for a fine piece (one time in four, once a lifetime, a Praag filigree chain), or decline.

title: The Observatory
summary: An astronomer of the old Observatory has read the stars over Kislev. Fund the readings, or send him back to his tower.

title: The missing servants
summary: Servants of the great houses go missing in the night. Look into it (the hunt begins), or let it be.

title: Never at dawn prayers
summary: A boyar of the Duma never comes to the dawn prayers, and never to a daytime feast. Keep watching (praag.42), or drop it.

title: The portrait
summary: In the boyar's house hangs a portrait of his great-grandfather. It is the boyar, to the last grey hair. The truth comes out (praag.43).

title: The boyars who do not age
summary: The vampire boyars are found out: the Upirnovs (von Carstein blood) or the Kalashinivik sisters (Lahmians). Purge them with the Circle of the Bear, bargain for gold and secrets (one of them stays at court), or be drawn in as their living thrall.

title: The Upirnov captain
summary: A pale boyar of the Upirnovs offers to keep the peace in Praag's streets. He is very good at it. Take him into service (a hidden vampire at court, Praag quieter for twenty years), or decline.

title: A Vasilikov's claim
summary: A Vasilikov arrives with a chest of old charters: his house, he says, held a quarter of Praag before the Tzarina's time. Recognise the claim (he joins the court with a claim on a city of Praag), refuse him, or throw him in the cells.

title: An opera about the reign
summary: The Opera House offers to stage an opera about the ruler. Commission it (a triumph, or a scandal if the librettist mocks you), or decline.

title: The diva
summary: The prima donna of the season wants a patron. Invite her to court, send flowers and jewels, or ignore her.

title: Murder in the boxes
summary: A boyar is found dead in his box during the third act, drained white. Investigate (a clever ruler may find the vampire boyars, praag.41), hush it up, or blame the Ungols.

title: The cult in the opera house
summary: Under the stage of the old opera house a Chaos cult meets between performances. Raid it (martial: the cult broken and doom eased a little, but the season is lost), let the Court Chekist break it quietly (intrigue), or close the house for a season and hope.

title: The Z'ra heirs
summary: When the crown of Kislev is weak, the heirs of the old Z'ra rulers come to Praag's lord with Ungol swords behind them. Champion them (stand for independence with the factions; a Z'ra heir joins the court), betray them to the Tzar(ina) (favour, gold, and the duchy of Praag if the crown holds it), or send them away.

title: The Geheimnisnacht Ball
summary: On startup, once a game (also curses the Cursed Company's first captain, undead.14): in a 2010 start, every living Sylvanian lord of Vlad's realm gets his invitation (undead.2). Vlad, if a player, hears how the night went (undead.3).

title: An invitation to Drakenhof
summary: A living lord of Sylvania attends Vlad's ball. He may take the Blood Kiss and become a von Carstein (from_makes_root_vampire_effect), kneel as a living thrall of the Court of Sylvania, or refuse.

title: The ball is over
summary: Vlad, a player, hears how the night went.

title: The barrow opens
summary: A master of the dead breaks open an old barrow and calls its champion back. One time in twenty the barrow held a king: a Wight King, who may bring his tomb blade.

title: The leash breaks
summary: A wight whose employer is no master of the dead, and serves none, falls back into dust (the captain of the Cursed Company is cursed, not bound, and lasts). Fired a day after a master dies (undead.12), so the wight is already at the heir's court, and every five years as a sweep.

title: A master of the dead dies
summary: The wights of his court are checked a day later (undead.11).

title: Dust
summary: The new master learns that a wight of the court has fallen into dust.

title: The captain of the Cursed Company
summary: Whoever leads the Cursed Company is a wight: the curse takes him the day he takes the banner. Fired for a new holder of d_the_cursed_company and at startup (undead.1).

title: Who will work the enchantment?
summary: Finds a necromancer of the realm and a Necrarch of the Brotherhood, then lets the lord choose. The work takes two weeks, two months or four months (undead.51).

title: The ritual is ready
summary: The lord chooses what to bind: a weapon or a suit of armour. The result follows at once (undead.52).

title: The binding
summary: A Necrarch never fails. A necromancer of the realm fails one time in ten, the lord himself one time in seven: the item survives, but the spell is lost. On success the item becomes a necromantic one of its kind (undead_enchant_weapon_effect, undead_enchant_armour_effect).

title: A sire's death
summary: When a vampire ruler dies, every vampire in the realm outside the dynasty (the thralls they made) gets a claim on the dead ruler's primary title (vamp.2).

title: Claim on the sire's title
summary: Hidden. Gives the thrall a claim on FROM's primary title.

title: A thrall asks for a duchy
summary: A landless or baron vampire made by a liege of their dynasty who holds two or more duchies asks the sire for one of them (vamp.4).

title: The thrall's request for a duchy
summary: The sire grants a duchy that is not their primary title (vamp.5) or refuses (vamp.6) and earns the thrall's lasting resentment.

title: Request granted
summary: The sire granted the request. Notification.

title: Request refused
summary: The sire refused the request. Notification.

title: A thrall asks for a county
summary: Like vamp.3, for an unlanded thrall whose sire holds four or more counties.

title: The thrall's request for a county
summary: The sire grants a county that is not their primary title (vamp.5) or refuses (vamp.6).

title: The blood kiss
summary: The turning decision used on someone under 16: the child is told who turned them and the sire is notified (vamp.11).

title: A new child of the night
summary: The child joins the ranks of the undead.

title: Jealous lover
summary: A vampire whose vampire lover keeps other lovers too demands to be the only one (vamp.16). The kind and charitable may choose to share.

title: An ultimatum
summary: The unfaithful lover either sends the other lovers away (vamp.18, vamp.19) or leaves the jealous one (vamp.17).

title: Spurned
summary: The jealous vampire was dropped and becomes the unfaithful lover's rival.

title: Only you
summary: The unfaithful lover chose the jealous vampire. A prestige reward.

title: Cast aside
summary: The other lovers are sent away and become the jealous vampire's rivals. jealous vampire.

title: The ring is taken
summary: Hidden. Passes the Carstein Ring decision on to whoever holds the ring's thief (vamp.21).

title: What to do with the ring?
summary: The holder of a stolen Carstein Ring may keep it (vampires only; gains claims on the old owner's titles if necromantic) or destroy it. Players hear about it (vamp.22 or vamp.612).

title: The ring has a new master
summary: Another vampire has taken the Carstein Ring. Notification for players.

title: The ring thief: the plotter's chance
summary: The head of a plot to steal the Carstein Ring sees an opening and hires a thief, paid by the plot backers, from their own purse or with their own cunning (learning). The thief strikes a month later (vamp.30).

title: The ring thief: a backer's chance
summary: A backer of the ring plot finds a thief and tells the plotter (vamp.35) or asks the plotter for funds (vamp.27).

title: Funds for the thief
summary: The plotter is asked to pay for the thief (vamp.28) or refuses (vamp.29).

title: Funds received
summary: The backer has the money and sends the thief in (vamp.30).

title: No funds
summary: The plotter refused to pay: the backer pays alone or gives up.

title: A touch in the death-sleep

title: Robbed, and the thief is known
summary: The ring is gone and the target knows who sent the thief, who may vanish with it (vamp.42) or keep it (vamp.21).

title: Robbed by an unknown thief
summary: The ring is gone; the plotters may keep it (vamp.21) or lose the thief (vamp.42).

title: The thief is caught
summary: The target wakes, catches the thief and learns the plotter's name.

title: The thief escapes
summary: The target wakes in time, but the thief escapes empty-handed.

title: A backer has a plan
summary: A backer found a thief and asks the plotter to go ahead (vamp.36).

title: Go ahead
summary: The plotter approves and the thief is sent (vamp.30).

title: The plot moves
summary: The other backers hear that the thief will act within a month.

title: Success, but exposed
summary: The ring is taken, but the plotter's part is known.

title: Success, unseen
summary: The ring is taken and nobody knows who sent the thief.

title: Failure, and exposed
summary: The thief was caught and named the plotter; the plot is revealed.

title: Failure, unseen
summary: The thief fled empty-handed; the plotters may try again.

title: The thief has vanished
summary: The thief disappeared with the ring, which is lost. Necromantic thieves lose prestige.

title: The Red Duke rises
summary: At game start the Red Duke of Aquitaine rises: retinues of Black Knights, Grave Guard and Blood Knights, and for the AI money and a Blood Knight host to start the war at once.

title: The band grows
summary: A Blood Dragon war band gathers new fledglings, bringing its founder prestige.

title: Spoils for the Grand Master
summary: A Blood Dragon mercenary captain sends trinkets from the quest to the master of the order (vamp.53). About once in 30 years per captain.

title: Tribute from the quest
summary: The master of the order receives the spoils, sometimes the blade of a fallen champion (artifact vamp_quest_trophy).

title: A worthy recruit
summary: A Blood Dragon mercenary captain picks a strong young courtier, or a child, of the employer's court, turns them and takes them away. The employer (vamp.55) and the band's founder (vamp.56) are told. About once in 30 years per captain.

title: A child stolen
summary: The employer learns that the mercenary turned and took one of the court.

title: A new knight of the order
summary: The band's founder learns of the new recruit.

title: The Blood Dragons dig in
summary: The Blood Dragons have started to occupy a province with a decision; a fortress will rise there in 250 days (vamp.58) unless the province is freed.

title: A Blood Dragon fortress
summary: If the occupation held, a castle is built in the province for the Blood Dragon.

title: Waking from hibernation

summary: A Strigoi ruler may swear fealty to the new Strygos (always if a Strigoi rules it).

title: The Strigany return
summary: Strigany settlers come back to a province of Strygos held by a Strigany.

title: Strygos is resettled
summary: Hidden. Every five years each province of the emperor's realm in Strygos may turn Strygan (vamp.75) or Strigany (vamp.76), each about once in 60 years.

summary: A small pack of war beasts.

summary: The crystal heals the decay and may give Lore of Heavens. A ruler may then receive a demand or a vision from the Dragon-Emperor (vamp.122).

summary: Treasures vanish from the treasury, sent to an unknown place on the vampire's own orders.

summary: Stewardship for some years (jade_plus_stewardship).

summary: Intrigue for some years (jade_plus_intrigue).

summary: Learning for some years (jade_plus_learning).

calls: vampsoc.221; vampsoc.222; vampsoc.223; vampsoc.224; vampsoc.225; vampsoc.226
title: Lahmian flavour
summary: Picks one Lahmian Sisterhood flavour event (vampsoc.221 - vampsoc.226).

title: A witch hunter asks questions
summary: A witch hunter has heard rumours about the beautiful lady who is never seen by day. Mislead him with Favour, have him killed (risky), or flee the court for a while.

title: A rival Sister
summary: Another Sister has been whispering against you to the Queen. Outwit her, or buy her silence.

title: A letter from the Silver Pinnacle
summary: The Queen of Mysteries asks a service: gold for a bribe in a distant court. Obey for Favour, or ignore her at a cost.

title: An admirer
summary: A mortal admirer begs for the honour of feeding you. Drink, or toy with them for the court's amusement.

title: The masked ball
summary: You host a masked ball, and the princes of the realm dance with you until dawn. Favour, and a small chance of the Cameo of Neferata.

title: The portrait
summary: A courtier has found an old portrait of you, painted sixty years ago, and you have not aged a day. Bribe them, kill them, or let them talk.

title: The Great Web
summary: The Queen of Mysteries sets out to bind the courts of the Old World to the Silver Pinnacle. Three to five years later: vampsoc.231.

title: The web is spun
summary: Every Sister gains Favour and the Queen rules the courts from her bed and her letters. For life.

title: The Magnum Opus
summary: The Necrarch begins the great work of their unlife. Two to four years later: vampsoc.251.

title: The work is done
summary: Learning decides the result. Success passes the trial with a reward by field; failure costs five years.

title: The hunt for a relic of Nagash
summary: A Master Necrarch sends an expedition into the deserts of Nehekhara for a relic of the Great Necromancer. Two to three years later: vampsoc.256.

title: The expedition returns
summary: The relic is found (a seat in the Dark Tower can now be claimed), the Tomb Kings drive the expedition off, or the desert takes it.

title: A Wight King rises
summary: A Master Necrarch binds the spirit of a barrow king back into his bones: a Wight King who serves as a commander (wight_rise_effect). He may bring his tomb blade (wight_tomb_blade_effect).

title: A breakthrough
summary: Every twenty years or so a Necrarch's long labour bears fruit.

calls: vampsoc.260; vampsoc.271; vampsoc.272; vampsoc.273; vampsoc.274; vampsoc.275; vampsoc.276
title: Necrarch flavour
summary: The breakthrough when it is due (vampsoc.260), else one Necrarch flavour event (vampsoc.271 - vampsoc.276).

title: A letter from the Tower
summary: Another Necrarch writes to dispute a point of necromantic theory. Answer at length, or ignore them.

title: The apprentice
summary: Your apprentice has made progress, or a terrible mistake.

title: Grave robbing
summary: Your servants need fresh bodies for your work. Rob your own graveyards, or buy corpses from beyond the border.

title: The tower grows
summary: You add a new floor to your tower: a laboratory, an ossuary, a library.

title: Forgotten notes
summary: In an old chest you find your own notes from three centuries ago, and perhaps a copy of a page of the Liber Mortis.

title: The peasants complain
summary: The peasants say the tower's lights burn all night and their dead do not stay buried. Placate them, or ignore them.

title: The Recipe for Nagash
summary: A Lord of the Dark Tower holding a relic of Nagash begins to reconstruct the Great Necromancer's work. Three to five years later: vampsoc.281.

title: The recipe is complete
summary: The Lord has reconstructed the Recipe for Nagash. A permanent mastery of death, and every Necrarch gains Lore.

title: The ghoul court
summary: The trial of the Strigoi: gather a court of ghouls, the cannibal wretches who live among the graves. One to two years later: vampsoc.301.

title: The court gathers
summary: The starving poor make a large court that is hard to hold; the graveyard-eaters make a small one that holds. Success passes the trial.

title: The curse of Ushoran
summary: A Strigoi who has gone hungry loses control and becomes the beast.

calls: vampsoc.310; vampsoc.321; vampsoc.322; vampsoc.323; vampsoc.324; vampsoc.325; vampsoc.326
title: Strigoi flavour
summary: A hungry Strigoi may fall into frenzy (vampsoc.310); otherwise one Strigoi flavour event (vampsoc.321 - vampsoc.326).

title: Scorned by the blood
summary: A vampire of another bloodline has called the Strigoi beasts and grave-eaters before witnesses. Swallow it, or answer in blood.

title: The caravan comes
summary: A Strigany caravan arrives with news, stolen goods and a cart of volunteers for the Strigoi's table.

title: The crypt feast
summary: The ghouls have dug up a fresh graveyard. Join the feast, or keep your dignity.

title: The dream of Strygos
summary: In the day-sleep you walk the marble halls of Strygos before it fell, and Ushoran speaks to you.

title: Digging in the ruins
summary: Your servants dig in the ruins of a Strygan city. Old gold, and perhaps the Bone Crown of Strygos.

title: Hunters on the trail
summary: Vampire hunters have tracked you to your lair. Fight them, or move on.

title: Strygos Reborn
summary: The Heir of Ushoran calls the scattered Strigoi to rebuild the court of Strygos. Three to four years later: vampsoc.331.

title: The court of Ushoran
summary: Strygos lives again in its king. For life, and every Strigoi gains Hunger.

title: The Scribe's Examination
summary: A Crystal Mandarin sits the examination of the Coil, a cruel mirror of the Imperial examinations: three days of questions put by the Sage's serpents.

title: Shedding the skin
summary: The Jade vampire coils in the dark of the crystal chamber and sheds the old skin, and the jade decay with it.

title: The Serpent's Coils
summary: The Serpent Sage winds a mortal ruler in the coils of the Jade Court: tribute now, and a lasting fascination.

calls: vampsoc.371; vampsoc.372; vampsoc.373; vampsoc.374; vampsoc.375; vampsoc.376
title: Jade flavour
summary: Picks one Jade Coil flavour event (vampsoc.371 - vampsoc.376).

title: The Imperial Scribe
summary: An Imperial Scribe arrives to count the taxes of the province. The Jade Coil has always found scribes delicious.

title: The itch beneath the scales
summary: The old skin grows tight. Bask by the crystal, or ignore it.

title: The crystal hums
summary: A small vision in the Dark Crystal: a lesson, or a hunger.

title: A rival Coil
summary: Another Jade vampire tries to hypnotise your servants. A duel of stares.

title: A crystal shard
summary: A servant brings a sliver of dark crystal found in a mountain stream: perhaps the Shard of the Dark Crystal.

title: The Emperor's hunters
summary: Agents of the Dragon Emperor are hunting the serpents again. Fight them in the dark, or slither away.

title: The Celestial Gaze
summary: The Serpent Sage coils around the greatest of the Dark Crystals and gazes at the whole of the heavens. Three to four years later: vampsoc.381.

title: The heavens seen
summary: The Sage has seen everything under heaven. For life, and every Coil gains Venom.

title: The Beloved
summary: The trial of the Carrion Children: a mortal has asked for you. Love them for a year, and then devour them. A year later: vampsoc.401.

title: The end of love
summary: Devour the Beloved and pass the trial, or spare them and fail it.

title: The Vigil at Gwingui
summary: An Elder of the Swarm keeps vigil at the gate of Gwingui, where the shadow realm touches the world. One to two years later: vampsoc.406.

title: What came through the gate
summary: The vigil ends. The gate has accepted the Elder (the mark of the next Big Bokor) or spat them out.

title: Devouring kin
summary: The Mahtmasi eats another vampire, as the Carrion Children do.

title: A dream sent
summary: The Mahtmasi sends a dream to a mortal ruler. They wake longing, and may come asking; or they wake screaming.

calls: vampsoc.421; vampsoc.422; vampsoc.423; vampsoc.424; vampsoc.425; vampsoc.426
title: Mahtmasi flavour
summary: Picks one Carrion Children flavour event (vampsoc.421 - vampsoc.426).

title: The swarm
summary: You come apart into flies and carrion birds and drift over the land, hearing everything.

title: Fire in the night
summary: The villagers have found your resting place and come with torches. The Mahtmasi fear fire above all.

title: A plea at the altar
summary: A mortal has left an offering at your altar and asks for gold, a child or a dead rival.

title: Maatmeses in dreams
summary: The first of the Mahtmasi, who lives now only in dreams, speaks to you.

title: Running water
summary: Your road crosses a river, and running water burns the Mahtmasi. Go the long way around, or be carried across.

title: The bokor's gift
summary: A bokor brings a fetish from the gate of Gwingui: perhaps the Bokor's Fetish itself.

title: Cast out the Westerlanders
summary: The Big Bokor turns the shadow realm against the Westerlanders of Sudenburg and the witch hunters of Samur. Two to three years later: vampsoc.431.

title: The shadows take Sudenburg
summary: The Westerlanders' hold on Sudenburg is broken. The lands of Sudenburg held by the Big Bokor or their vassals are haunted for good; every Mahtmasi gains Offerings.

title: Another bloodline
summary: A vampire ruler of another bloodline holds lands nearby. The bloodlines have hated each other since Lahmia fell, but a pact can serve both. event_target:vampsoc_other is a vampire ruler of another bloodline.

title: Fightier
summary: One stack of fightiness for a battle or war won (AI rulers get two longer stacks and more prestige).

title: A major victory
summary: Two stacks of fightiness for a major battle won (three for the AI).

title: A lost battle
summary: Fightiness drops by two for a lost battle (the AI may be spared).

title: A major defeat
summary: Fightiness drops by three for a major battle lost (the AI may be spared).

title: A lost war
summary: Fightiness drops by three for a war lost or a white peace (the AI may be spared).

title: Da call grows
summary: A major victory in a WAAAGH! war adds to the call to WAAAGH!.

title: Da call fades
summary: A major defeat in a WAAAGH! war shrinks the call to WAAAGH!.

title: Da boyz want a WAAAGH!
summary: An independent greenskin ruler with fightiness 15 or more is asked to call a WAAAGH!. He can refuse three times (each refusal costs prestige); the fourth time he must call it or become a squatter king. Calling it turns fightiness into WAAAGH! empowerment and starts waaagh.11.

title: WAAAGH!
summary: The ruler takes the WAAAGH! government, gets a WAAAGH! empire title, boyz, manpower and population for his holdings, and two years to start the WAAAGH! war. The AI starts it within a year (waaagh.13).

title: A WAAAGH! is coming
summary: Tells the target and nearby rulers that a WAAAGH! has been declared.

title: WAAAGH!!!
summary: An AI warlord launches his WAAAGH!: more boyz, a large army, prestige and piety.

title: You waited too long
summary: A WAAAGH! government warlord who has not started a WAAAGH! war in time and is no longer fighty enough loses the WAAAGH!: back to tribal government, his king and emperor titles are destroyed, some boyz stay. Players with 1000 prestige can pay to wait longer.

title: The march (every six months)
summary: Runs for the leader of every WAAAGH! war about every six months, from the start of the war until it ends. Wears the warlord out over time, sends a small defender to its fate (waaagh.35), and rolls a march event for every greenskin commander in the defender's lands.

title: Another boss on da march
summary: A player meets another boss of the same WAAAGH! on the march and is asked to his camp for grog and roast squig: make a friend, or show off by krumpin' a few of his boyz.

title: A caravan on da road
summary: The wolf riders spot a merchant caravan near the camp. Raid it for loot, make it pay a toll, send the gobbos in to nick the shiny stuff at night, or let it go. The loot can be a piece of greenskin loot an' plunder or a treasure of the land being raided (waaagh_loot_artifact_effect).

title: A comet
summary: A comet over the camp. Lead the boyz as an omen of Gork, drive them as a taskmaster, or (after both) take advice from a snotling who claims the comet chose him, and make him marshal.

title: Guided by Gork or by grog
summary: The commander claims divine guidance... or was it the drink?

title: A wandering warband
summary: A player meets a greenskin mercenary warband on the march: befriend, insult, hire some of the boyz, or (for great warlords) take them as vassals.

title: Warriors gather
summary: Boyz flock to the WAAAGH!. Reinforcements or manpower, more the fightier the commander.

title: Warriors gather (big)
summary: As waaagh.26, bigger, with a retinue option.

title: Empowered by the WAAAGH!
summary: Fightiness or the call to WAAAGH! turns into WAAAGH! empowerment.

title: Sack the town
summary: A WAAAGH! warlord who takes a holding of the defender can sack it (gold and a chance of loot, buildings burnt, people killed, cruel) or spare it.

title: The WAAAGH! is upon us
summary: A small king or emperor targeted by a WAAAGH! must hold his realm together at a price, or give in: the war ends and his top titles are destroyed.

title: The mighty have fallen
summary: Tells the warlord and the players that a WAAAGH! target gave in.

title: A lieutenant wants land
summary: A landless or low-tier greenskin in a WAAAGH! realm asks the warlord for a county (two or more counties and modest prestige needed). Players can instead leave their demesne unmanaged.

title: Give the lieutenant land?
summary: The warlord gives a county (outside his capital kingdom or duchy if he can, made tribal), or refuses.

title: The WAAAGH! ends
summary: The heir of a dead WAAAGH! warlord who is not strong enough keeps the WAAAGH! only if he is a Black Orc; otherwise the WAAAGH! breaks up.

title: The prestige is shared
summary: Tells the heir and his siblings that the dead warlord's prestige was split.

title: A new war leader
summary: Under military elective succession the heir gets part of the wealth, the artifacts and the titles (the Brass Legion's heir becomes a Chaos champion). Not only greenskins use this.

title: Titles pass on
summary: Gives the dead leader's flagged titles to the heir.

title: A new greenskin realm
summary: Tells players that a lieutenant now rules the conquered region.

title: The horde migrates
summary: Tells players that a WAAAGH! horde migrated to its conquest.

title: The warlord takes the land
summary: Tells players that a warlord kept the conquered region.

summary: From the warband_khorne_berserker decision.

title: A recruit joins
summary: The warband of the recruit's god (Undivided worshippers, and Beastmen in particular, may choose one god), Gork or Mork by temper (brutal or kunnin' traits), or the Skaven Warlords. The first member becomes the leader. Rank-4 players hear of it (warband.62).

title: A fallen warband rises again
summary: From on_society_destroyed (common/on_actions/00_on_actions_warbands.txt). A fitting courtier or vassal of the last member (or of their liege) takes up the banner and leads it.

title: The war sacrifice
summary: From warband_war_sacrifice (the warbands but Gork and Mork, and the Warriors of Ulric): an offering for victory, in the way of each power. Undivided, Slaanesh and the Skaven offer kin, a servant or slave, or plunder; Khorne wants a champion's blood in a duel to the death, or skulls and plunder; Tzeentch takes kin and pays out as fate decides; Nurgle shares his gifts with kin, the champion or a whole province. Ulric takes no lives: an oath sworn in blood before the flame, or the spoils burned in it. The stronger the offering, the stronger the war blessing (lodge_war_sacrifice_2 - 4, five years); ten years must pass before the next. Scope: the champion.

title: The war host sees the offering
summary: The warriors roar; a Warrior of Ulric or a Norscan veteran may take the lodge's tattoos. Scope: the champion.

title: A war starts
summary: From on_war_started. A warband or lodge member on either side looks for a player of the same society to ask for help (waraid.2 or waraid.3).

title: The defender asks for help
summary: If the player refuses and the attacker shares the society, the attacker makes a counter-offer (waraid.3).

title: The attacker asks for help
summary: Either the first ask (waraid.1) or a counter-offer after the player turned down the defender (waraid.2, flag waraid_spurned_defender).

title: The attacker wins
summary: From on_war_ended_victory. Each player who fought beside one side hears the outcome from their ally (waraid.13).

title: White peace
summary: From on_war_ended_whitepeace. Each player who fought beside one side hears the outcome from their ally (waraid.13).

title: The defender wins
summary: From on_war_ended_defeat. Each player who fought beside one side hears the outcome from their ally (waraid.13).

title: The ally writes after the war
summary: Won: glory, perhaps a celebration (waraid.14) or, rarely, veterans (waraid.16). Held: some glory. Failed or lost: scorn.

title: The victory celebration
summary: Each society celebrates its own way: a pit fight before the altar, a Skaven feast (bring your own food), a greenskin brawl, an Ulrican hunt, a tourney, a dawi drinking bout. Winning may lead to waraid.15.

title: Letters after the celebration
summary: Restored from vanilla (HF.50106, never sent): the ally keeps writing.

title: The veterans arrive
summary: Rarely, once in a life, after a victory the ally sends a company of veterans to serve the player for good (half upkeep).

title: A province bears the taint of Chaos
summary: A ruler with a Chaos-tainted demesne province (Nurgle disease, beastmen, warpdust, warpstone, Slaanesh hedonism) decides whether to send their court witch hunter after it. Cultist rulers may refuse.

title: Evil stirs
summary: The witch hunter receives the call for help and sets out. Province events that fire this save the ruler as event_target:whunter_client.

title: The witch hunter arrives
summary: The ruler welcomes the witch hunter to court.

title: Time to get to work
summary: The witch hunter starts a three-year hunt at the ruler's court and moves there unless they already hold a court witch hunter title.

title: The investigation is finished
summary: After three years the hunt ends. The witch hunter gains skill, tells the liege, and goes home.

title: The witch hunter reports
summary: The witch hunter reports to the ruler; the purge marker leaves the province.

title: A suspicious courtier
summary: A witch hunter on a hunt picks a suspicious-looking courtier of their liege (mutated, ugly, lustful, mystic...) and confronts them. list).

title: Hunting suspected cultists
summary: A witch hunter on a hunt goes after a courtier of their liege who is under suspicion, highly suspect or a known satanist. The confrontation goes on as for whunter.10 (whunter.12).

title: The courtier is confronted
summary: The accused courtier answers the witch hunter. Their Intrigue and Learning, known suspicion, and magic laws for mages decide whether the hunter believes them. Reached from whunter.10 and 11; the investigation (whunter.176) also uses it to confront unlanded suspects.

title: Not a heretic
summary: The witch hunter is convinced the courtier is innocent, but may still accuse.

title: A heretic
summary: The witch hunter is convinced the courtier is a heretic and accuses them.

title: The accused appeals
summary: The accused courtier hears the charge. An independent ruler deals with the witch hunter directly; anyone else appeals to their liege.

title: The liege decides
summary: The liege chooses: burn the accused, imprison them, or spare them. When the accusation is upheld the hunter gains piety, may learn from the case, and Order members earn currency; mission hunters are paid or fined by the Order depending on the verdict. Also the verdict for hunt quarries (whunter.192).

title: Burned at the stake
summary: The accused is burned. Shared verdict: also fired by the mage hunt (whunter.152) and by Chaos and mutation events.

title: Imprisoned
summary: The liege imprisons the accused. Shared verdict, as whunter.17.

title: Spared
summary: The liege intervenes and the witch hunter backs off. Shared verdict, as whunter.17.

title: A noble burned
summary: Players in the realm hear that a landed noble was burned by the witch hunters. They can choose not to hear about it again.

title: Cleansing the taint
summary: A court witch hunter on a hunt removes the Chaos taint from one of the liege's provinces.

title: The taint is gone
summary: The liege hears the taint has been removed; the taint modifiers leave one tainted province.

title: Vampires in the realm
summary: An idle witch hunter warns the top liege that vampires walk openly in the realm, unless the liege allows vampires. (whunter_realm_heretics list).

title: The hunters come for the vampires
summary: The top liege calls the hunt. Strong vampires (Martial or Intrigue 15) escape once; the others are burned.

title: A vampire escapes
summary: The vampire flees the realm and remembers the lucky escape.

title: A vampire burns
summary: The vampire is burned at the stake.

title: Chaos worshippers in the realm

title: A Chaos worshipper escapes
summary: The worshipper flees the realm and remembers the lucky escape.

title: A Chaos worshipper burns
summary: The worshipper is burned at the stake.

title: No witch hunters in the realm
summary: A ruler above count rank with no witch hunter anywhere in the realm can hire two from the local chapter; the elder takes the empty court seat. Players can refuse for good.

title: Heretics leave
summary: An unlanded Chaos worshipper or open vampire in an Old World realm whose liege does not share their faith moves to a ruler of their own faith (or, for a vampire, to a vampire lord) outside the Old World faiths.

title: A Grand Master dies
summary: Under elective succession the heir takes over and gets gold and prestige. If the heir holds a chapter seat, the council picks a new Knight-Captain (whunter.51).

title: Call the council
summary: Opens the council choice for the new Grand Master.

title: The Witch Hunter's council
summary: The new Grand Master picks a Knight-Captain for the seat they left, from up to four rank 2 members.

title: A chapter master dies
summary: A chapter seat holder dies without elective succession: a fit witch hunter in their court inherits the seat (whunter.54), or a new one is made.

title: Inheritance
summary: The heir receives the dead master's chapter seat and joins the Order.

title: An independent chapter master dies
summary: The designated Knight-Captain heir takes over the chapter; otherwise the heir keeps the congregation government and takes the oath (whunter.56).

title: The heir takes the oath
summary: The heir of an independent chapter becomes a witch hunter and joins the Order.

title: Find a Knight-Captain heir
summary: Picks a fit Knight-Captain heir from the court, or makes a new witch hunter, and hands the chapter over (whunter.58). master is relieved of command.

title: Master accused of bad conduct
summary: The accused's traits and piety set the starting proof, then the Council Knights vote (whunter.62) and the Grand Master gives the verdict (whunter.63).
